name: 24 Hour Fitness - Sugar Land
description: Get your sweat on at 24 Hour Fitness in Sugar Land, a convenient gym on Highway 6 for Houston area fitness buffs. Ideal for focused workouts in a suburban setting.
review: Been coming to 24 Hour Fitness in Sugar Land for years, but it disappoints with unfriendly staff who ignore you when you walk in, where’s the customer service? A few male staff and trainers are nice, but most aren’t.

name: 59 Diner
description: Step back in time at 59 Diner in Stafford, a nostalgic Stafford diner serving gooey grilled cheese sandwiches and thick malts.
review: 59 DINER! My friends, sister, and I came here late at night, after enjoying ourselves at a concert. Right when we stepped in, I felt as if I had been transported to the 'happy days' years.

name: A Sweet Factory
description: A Sweet Factory, a hidden spot in Houston on Westheimer Road, serves gooey kanafeh and fragrant Arabian pastries.
review: A Sweet Factory in Houston is a dessert gem! Love the Mediterranean pastries, kanafeh is my favorite, a bright orange, cheesy delight with oozing mozzarella and akawi, topped with sweet syrup when warmed.

name: Abdallah’s Bakery
description: Abdallah’s Bakery, a cozy spot in Houston’s Gulfton on Hillcroft Street, serves falafel wraps and lemony spinach pastries.
review: Abdallah’s Bakery in Houston’s Gulfton is a Lebanese gem, though hit or miss! This small spot on Hillcroft has tight parking but great food.

name: Acacia Food Mart
description: Embark on a culinary journey at Acacia Food Mart, a Fondren Southwest gem bringing authentic Turkish and international flavors to Houston.
review: I enjoyed my time at Acacia food market this week. This market is a little small, but you’ll be sure to find most things here that are Turkish/European/International.

name: Afandim Restaurant
description: Embark on a unique culinary journey at Afandim Restaurant in Houston’s Chinatown, where authentic Uyghur cuisine shines on Bellaire Boulevard.
review: Tasty and authentic Uyghur cuisine in Houston! My friends and I all had lunch here about 3 weeks ago. We were all warmly welcomed and were so excited to try many different dishes.

name: Agha Juice And Cafe
description: Agha Juice And Cafe, a grab and go spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, serves creamy falooda shakes with rose syrup and kulfi.
review: Agha Juice And Cafe in Sugar Land is a Houston area grab and go gem! Not a sit down spot, but perfect for creamy South Asian shakes and ice cream.

name: Agora
description: Agora, a beloved spot in Houston’s Montrose on Westheimer Road, serves aromatic gingerbread lattes and crispy melomakarana cookies.
review: Agora in Montrose is one of Houston’s greatest coffee shops, I’ve been coming for years! Tried a holiday gingerbread latte recently, and it was a delight, not overly sweet like typical seasonal drinks.

name: Aki Steak & Sushi
description: Aki Steak & Sushi in Sugar Land is a suburban gem on Highway 6, offering all day happy hour specials on Sundays that draw Houston families and foodies alike.
review: I’m liking the happy hour specials on Sunday, which are all day! My sister and friends were just here last weekend and we all enjoyed our dinner.

name: Al Rabba World Food
description: Al Rabba World Food brings a wide ranging, multicultural grocery experience to a quiet corner of Sugar Land.
review: I’m not sure where the low ratings are coming from, I had a nice experience today.

name: ALDI
description: Discover wallet friendly shopping at ALDI in Meadows Place, a German super chain market on FM 2234 that’s a hit for Houston area bargain hunters.
review: I’ve been frequenting ALDI for a while, and it’s great to have a location closer to Sugar Land! They’re a small German super chain market that’s sprouted all around the US.

name: All About Cakes
description: All About Cakes, a charming spot in Sugar Land on Eldridge Road, serves moist banana pudding and red velvet cupcakes.
review: All About Cakes in Sugar Land makes this town sweeter! Visited with my sisters just before closing, staff and Chef Michelle warmly welcomed us despite the late hour.

name: Alpha Dessert Juice Cafe
description: Cool off with a sweet treat at Alpha Dessert Juice Cafe on Hillcroft in Houston’s Gulfton area, a vibrant spot showcasing Pakistani culture with murals and creamy kulfi.
review: Alpha Dessert Juice Cafe has expanded and looks totally different inside since my last rare visit. Love the murals and photos of Pakistani culture, such a great touch for a café like this.

name: Amorino Gelato
description: Amorino brings a touch of European indulgence to Highland Village, offering artisanal gelato and sorbet crafted with premium ingredients, many imported from around the world.
review: Ahh! I'm a big fan of sorbet… and this place totally satisfied my craving for all things sorbet related. Amorino serves authentic gelato, waffles, chocolates, coffee beverages, and even pound cakes and macarons.

name: Amy Hieu Hair Salon
description: Amy Hieu Hair Salon is a trusted neighborhood spot in Alief known for its natural approach to hair coloring, warm customer service, and an experienced stylist who genuinely cares about preserving hair health.
review: I got my hair colored a warm chocolate brown… and I’m loving it. The tones complement my jet brown hair beautifully, with layers blending in naturally. Amy is an artist when it comes to color, balayage, and ombré.

name: Amy’s Ice Creams
description: A long loved Texas favorite, Amy’s Ice Creams has always been known for quirky culture and creative mix ins, but this Upper Kirby visit reflects a shift that regulars are beginning to notice.
review: No longer a fan of this popular ice cream spot. I was just here two nights ago and the line was out the door. The two young dudes slingin' ice cream had no clue what they were doing.

name: Anatolia Int’l Foods
description: Anatolia Int’l Foods, a clean shop in Sugar Land on Highway 6, offers fresh meats, Turkish Nutella, and exotic spices. Grab Ulker hazelnut spread for a treat.
review: Anatolia Int’l Foods in Sugar Land didn’t start with warm customer service, but after a few visits, the owner warmed up to me and my family.

name: Anonymous Café
description: Step into the charming Anonymous Café in Sugar Land, a cozy Greek style coffee house on University Boulevard.
review: I’ve been coming to Anonymous Café since last summer, and they never disappoint! Love this cozy Greek style coffee house in Sugar Land. It’s small, but that adds to the charm with just a few tables and a comfy sofa chair.

name: Arnaldo Richard’s Picos
description: Arnaldo Richard’s Picos has long been a recognizable name in Houston’s Mexican and Tex Mex dining scene, especially in the bustling Upper Kirby neighborhood.
review: I thought the food here was just okay. The service was incredibly spotty and it was incredibly loud inside the restaurant. I had to flag down the waiter a few times and the food came out pretty slowly.

name: Ashar’s Kitchen
description: Grab flavorful halal dishes at Ashar’s Kitchen in Sugar Land, a Houston area spot perfect for takeaway beef biryani and naan.
review: I simply cannot comment on the interior of this restaurant.. nor on their service. Ashar’s Kitchen seems to be the place to grab and go food.. perfect for take away. Judging by the pictures..

name: Asia Blue
description: Asia Blue brings a fresh, modern presence to Tang City Plaza, pairing sleek décor with an open kitchen and a digital menu that makes browsing fun and easy.
review: I wanted to really love this new spot! The vibe is charming, modern interior, clean and sparkly décor, and an open kitchen where you can watch the chefs at work.

name: Asia Market Thai Lao Food
description: Asia Market Thai Lao Food in Houston’s The Heights, a cozy hole in the wall on North Main Street, serves homemade vegetarian pad kee mao and curry puffs.
review: Yum! Asia Market in The Heights serves delicious, authentic Thai food that stands out among Houston’s Thai spots.

name: Baklava Cafe
description: Baklava Cafe, a cozy spot in Sugar Land on University Boulevard, serves juicy chicken shawarma and fresh baklava.
review: Baklava Cafe in Sugar Land is a Houston area gem! Been coming since they opened, love their variety: sandwiches, pastas, salads, soups! The chicken shawarma is my favorite, with juicy meat and great toppings.

name: BAMBU
description: Cool off at BAMBU in Stafford’s Fountains Plaza, a clean and quiet café serving unique coconut cream tea with boba and authentic Vietnamese drinks like lychee smoothies.
review: Nice little spot at BAMBU in Stafford’s Fountains Plaza! There are other BAMBU locations in Houston, but this one’s clean and quieter. My favorite is the coconut cream tea with boba, not your typical coconut milk tea.

name: Bayou City Seafood and Pasta
description: Dive into the bold flavors of Bayou City Seafood and Pasta, a casual Highland Village spot that brings Cajun and Creole vibes to Houston.
review: I had the chance to try out Bayou City Seafood & Pasta earlier this week. Came here to have dinner with friends on a chilly Monday night. The outside of the restaurant looks quite shabby like a barbeque restaurant.

name: Beans Cafe CoffeeHouse
description: Unwind at Beans Cafe CoffeeHouse in Houston’s Energy Corridor, a cozy spot in a lively plaza on Dairy Ashford Road.
review: Beans Cafe CoffeeHouse is a cute little spot in a lively Energy Corridor plaza. Visited on a cold, dark Friday evening after work, drawn by curiosity. The ambiance, music, and mixed furniture designs were so appealing!

name: Bella Coffee & Gelato
description: Bella Coffee & Gelato, a cozy spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, serves cardamom salted caramel gelato with a fusion twist.
review: Bella Coffee & Gelato in Sugar Land was a delightful stop after eating at next door Bombay Pizza Express, same owners, so you get 10% off here! Limited seating but comfy vibe.

name: bellagreen
description: bellagreen, an elegant spot in Sugar Land’s Town Center, serves vegetarian minestrone soup and quinoa tabbouleh salad.
review: bellagreen in Sugar Land (formerly Ruggles Green) is a Houston area gem! Visited before Christmas with a friend and loved the elegant, organic vibe, nature paintings and a tree in the corner!

name: Bering’s
description: Bering’s is the kind of Houston staple that makes browsing feel like an adventure, warm, whimsical, and full of treasures across every aisle.
review: I stumbled upon a potato cookbook at Berings which will be perfect for bébé and I. Gotta love a good and hearty potato recipe, especially with cozy autumn around the corner.

name: BerriBlends
description: BerriBlends, a tidy spot in Richmond near Sugar Land, serves tart yogurt with customizable fruit toppings.
review: BerriBlends in Richmond is a Houston area gem! This tidy yogurt shop offers four flavors, and I love customizing with tart and four berry yogurt, topped with strawberries, blueberries, blackberries, and shredded mango.

name: Berripop Frozen Yogurt
description: Berripop Frozen Yogurt in Houston’s Meyerland Plaza on Beechnut Street offers crisp pomegranate yogurt with a variety of fruit toppings. Grab a pomegranate yogurt and enjoy the tangy delight.
review: Rarely in Meyerland, but I was thrilled to spot Berripop in the shopping plaza while wandering.

name: Berripop Frozen Yogurt
description: Berripop Frozen Yogurt, a bright spot in Houston’s West University on Kirby Drive, offers dark chocolate and snickerdoodle yogurt swirls with a new hot tea selection.
review: Berripop Frozen Yogurt in West University is a Houston favorite! The ample space, bright interior, and great service make it a go to.

name: Berripop Frozen Yogurt
description: Berripop Frozen Yogurt, a colorful spot in Sugar Land on University Boulevard, serves tart watermelon and black cherry yogurt.
review: Berripop Frozen Yogurt in Sugar Land is a Houston area gem! Love the tart, fruity flavors, watermelon and black cherry are standouts, and all flavors are great.

name: Berryhill Baja Grill
description: Berryhill Baja Grill, a lively spot in Houston’s Galleria on Westheimer Road, serves cheesy spinach enchiladas and fish tacos.
review: Berryhill Baja Grill in Houston’s Galleria serves solid Baja California cuisine! Tried the fish tacos and cheese spinach enchiladas, hot, cheesy, and generously filled.

name: Best Donuts
description: Best Donuts, a beloved spot in Sugar Land on University Boulevard, serves light cruller donuts and apple fritters.
review: Best Donuts in Sugar Land serves tasty donuts! I tried the cruller, cake donuts, and apple fritter, fresh, light in color, and not too sweet, with a nice appeal.

name: Bevers Kitchen & Gifts
description: Bevers Kitchen & Gifts captures everything you want from a countryside eatery, warm hospitality, hearty homestyle dishes, and a dessert selection that will make any pie lover swoon.
review: What a wonderful and cozy homestyle kitchen in the countryside. I loved it here and loved everything about Bevers Kitchen & Gifts.

name: Big Guy’s Chicken & Rice
description: Big Guy’s Chicken & Rice brings the spirit of classic New York street carts straight into Deep Ellum, bold flavors, big portions, and comfort you can count on.
review: Got a big appetite? Big Guy’s delivers. This spot serves up chicken and rice done right, spicy, comforting, and very reminiscent of New York style street food.

name: Bijan Persian Grill
description: Bijan Persian Grill, located on Hilcroft in Sharpstown, is a vibrant Sharpstown eatery serving juicy koobideh kebabs and exotic saffron ice cream.
review: Kebabs and Rice! As simple and yet so flavourful as it can get. That is all I need when I come to Bijan Persian Grill. The location is right on Hilcroft, towards the entrance. You can’t miss it.

name: Bijan Persian Grill
description: A Persian grill in Sugar Land serving traditional kebabs, stews, and saffron rice.
review: Bijan Persian Grill in Sugar Land was a letdown due to terrible customer service. The waiters were moody and unresponsive, never checking on me or my sister.

name: Bismillah Restaurant & Café
description: Bismillah Restaurant & Café has transformed its space with a brighter, cleaner, and more expansive layout, perfect for families, groups, and anyone craving halal comfort food with a South Asian twist.
review: I had dinner at Bismillah Café with my mother last night. I specifically came because I heard about the recent renovations, and I hadn’t been in ages. The restaurant is now in a bigger space with a cleaner, brighter look.

name: BJ’s Restaurant & Brewhouse
description: BJ’s Restaurant & Brewhouse, a spacious spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, serves pizza and American fare in a Chili’s like ambiance.
review: BJ’s Restaurant & Brewhouse in Sugar Land is a Houston area spot with a big Chili’s vibe. Sadly, the deep dish pizza disappointed, not hearty, thick, or loaded, just skimpy and frail.

name: Black Bear Diner
description: Black Bear Diner in Sugar Land wraps guests in a warm, nostalgic embrace, bringing the forested charm of Northern California straight into Texas.
review: BBD... aka Black Bear Diner.. such a cozy spot that reminds me of GoldiLocks and the three bears... except this bear theme is originating from Nor'Cal. Hence the theme of alll the northern trees and Nor'Cal Diner Vibes..

name: Black Hole Coffee House
description: Tucked in a quiet corner of Houston’s vibrant Museum District, Black Hole Coffee House is a quirky gem that draws coffee lovers with its chill vibe and homemade syrups.
review: I’ve been visiting Black Hole more often than usual now... lattes are still good.. quite milky and creamy. Vanilla latte being my favorite here. This place is usually packed in the afternoon.

name: Black Walnut Café
description: Enjoy a cozy meal at Black Walnut Café in Sugar Land on Highway 6, a local favorite for breakfast burritos, brioche French toast, and vegetarian pasta.
review: Service and food at Black Walnut Café have downgraded. Ordered a brownie and café latte on a Friday night, but the young lady taking our order disappeared, and another took over, both seemed scatterbrained.

name: Blacksmith
description: Blacksmith, a trendy spot in Houston’s Montrose on Westheimer Road, serves rich, deep flavored coffee with stunning latte art.
review: If coffee could be sexy, Blacksmith in Montrose nails it! This Houston spot serves rich, deep flavored coffee with subtle yet powerful notes, no acidic aftertaste.

name: Blenders
description: Blenders, a cozy spot in Houston’s Alief on Bellaire Boulevard, serves bold Vietnamese iced coffee and Thai iced tea with tapioca.
review: Blenders in Houston’s Alief is a tapioca gem, but I’m picky about pearls, they need that ‘al dente’ chew! Tried Cafe Su Dau, a fantastic Vietnamese iced coffee, sweet and intense, though it jittered me on an empty stomach.

name: BlendIn Coffee Club
description: Discover BlendIn Coffee Club, a sleek and modern coffee gem in the heart of Sugar Land, perfect for Houstonians craving a serious coffee experience.
review: I first visited BlendIn Coffee Club two months ago when they had just opened. It’s a new café in Sugar Land that’s tucked away in a quiet neighborhood.

name: Blue Fish House II
description: Dive into fresh Sugar Land sushi at Blue Fish House II, a casual Sugar Land spot serving hearty udon noodle soup and light avocado rolls.
review: It’s almost been a year since this establishment has been opened. It is nice to see that they are doing well. I like the atmosphere of this casual restaurant. I have tried the splendid ‘Udon it’ noodle soup.

name: Blue Willow Bookshop
description: Dive into a world of stories at Blue Willow Bookshop in Houston’s Energy Corridor, a cozy independent bookstore offering a curated selection of titles.
review: Unfriendly service. I walked inside the book store and the owner did not even acknowledge my presence. Just a calculating stare. Someone walked into the store literally right after me and she greets them.

name: Bombay Pizza Express
description: Bombay Pizza Express, a lively spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, serves crispy tandoori paneer rolls and veggie burgers with sweet potato fries.
review: Bombay Pizza Express in Sugar Land is a Houston area gem! Knew their downtown location but finally tried this closer spot twice last week.

name: Bombay to Beijing
description: Bombay to Beijing, a unique spot in Sugar Land’s Sugar Creek Plaza, serves creamy chicken tikka masala and wonton noodle soup.
review: Bombay to Beijing in Sugar Land is a Houston area gem for Indian Chinese fusion! Love the unique concept, neighboring cuisines in one spot! The decor blends bold Indian and Oriental vibes with rich paintings.

name: Bonchon
description: Discover Bonchon, a casual South Korean restaurant in Sugar Land that feels like home, tucked in a quiet plaza near Whole Foods.
review: Had the chance to try out Bonchon about two weeks ago with a good friend of mine. It’s tucked in a nice and quiet plaza near Whole Foods Sugar Land.

name: Boomtown Coffee
description: Boomtown Coffee, a lively spot in Houston’s The Heights on Yale Street, serves a standout honey milk latte and hosts poetry nights.
review: Boomtown Coffee in The Heights is a great Houston coffeehouse with unique drinks, my favorite’s the honey milk latte! They host poetry nights, which are perfect for unwinding with local poetic artists.

name: Bouchée Patisserie
description: A dreamy, candy land meets Paris patisserie nestled inside the Post Oak Hotel, Bouchée Patisserie is a visual and culinary escape.
review: Dream land… candy land… a whimsical pastry boutique of sorts. Walk in at anytime and you'll be fascinated upon the selection of tempting treats.

name: Brasil
description: Brasil has been a longstanding neighborhood fixture in Montrose, casual, artsy, and effortlessly cool in that old school Houston way.
review: I’ve been visiting this café for well over a decade and things really haven’t changed much. I recently visited twice, thinking the service was top notch.

name: British Isles
description: British Isles, a quaint shop in Houston’s West University on Rice Boulevard, offers teas, custard biscuits, and Lyle’s golden syrup. Grab a teapot or golden syrup.
review: British Isles in Rice Village is a lovely, quaint shoppe I’d always wanted to visit, and it didn’t disappoint!

name: Buc-ee’s
description: This location is built for speedy in and out visits, perfect for grabbing a hot drink, stocking up on road trip snacks, or fueling up before heading back toward Sugar Land or the surrounding areas.
review: This is just a simple and quick grab n’ go Buc ee’s. If you're randomly craving their in store snacks and treats, you'll find that here. They have the usual assortment of hot coffee, deli items and baked goods.

name: Cafe 101
description: Cafe 101, a colorful spot in Houston’s Chinatown on Bellaire Boulevard, serves fragrant lychee pearl tea and udon shrimp.
review: Cafe 101 in Houston’s Chinatown is a vibrant gem! Visited with friends on a bustling Thursday, loving the brilliant colors and cute decor.

name: Cafe Dolce Gelato
description: Tucked near Nordstrom in Houston’s Galleria, Cafe Dolce Gelato is a charming Italian inspired spot for coffee lovers and dessert enthusiasts.
review: I specifically came for the Illy coffee today. Needed a boost of caffeine and warmth from my latte while taking a stroll inside the Galleria. Illy is one of my favorite coffee brands emerging from Italia.

name: Cafe Marrese
description: The standout London fog latte, with its bergamot kissed foam, is a must try for tea lovers.
review: What a gross spot. 1 star breakfast experience. The saving grace for 2 stars? The London fog latte. That’s the only item we enjoyed during our stay here.

name: Caffè Bene
description: Discover a unique coffee experience at Caffè Bene in Downtown Houston, nestled in the Houston Pavilions on Main Street.
review: Tried Caffè Bene when it newly opened in Houston, and I was so happy they brought a location to HTX! Having enjoyed it in NYC, I wondered why we didn’t have one sooner.

name: Café Bustelo
description: A bright yellow shipping container café bringing the spirit of Latin coffee culture to Montrose, this pop up radiates personality, bold espresso, and a nostalgic nod to Gregorio Menendez Bustelo’s iconic coffee legacy.
review: You'll spot this bright yellow shipping container situated in the Montrose neighborhood. I was here about two weeks ago and made it just in time for a crisp iced beverage.

name: Campesino Coffee House
description: Unwind at Campesino Coffee House in Houston’s eclectic Montrose neighborhood, a cozy spot on Westheimer Road serving smooth café de olla, fresh juices, and delightful pastries.
review: Cozy, comfortable, and non pretentious at Campesino Coffee House, just how I like my coffee houses! Visited on a cloudy, rainy evening in Montrose, and three hours flew by.

name: Carmelo’s Mexican Grill
description: Carmelo’s Mexican Grill in Sugar Land serves oversized grande burritos and addictive crispy tortilla chips with garlicky salsa.
review: Que ricoo! :) Carmelo’s dishes up authentic burritos, tacos, enchiladas, and so forth.. you name it. I ordered the vegetarian burrito. Whoah, was it good! I’m never looking back at Chipotle! Well... unless..

name: Carter’s
description: This standalone Carter’s in Sugar Land is a breath of fresh air for parents who prefer to shop in person rather than rely solely on online browsing.
review: This is such a wonderful location of Carter's; from the warm customer service to the vivid selection of clothing they've got for tots and babes.

name: Casian King Food Truck
description: Casian King Food Truck, a vibrant mobile eatery in Houston’s Fourth Ward, serves Cajun Asian fusion like lobster fries and shrimp scampi.
review: Casian King Food Truck in the Fourth Ward served up tasty Cajun Asian fusion at Asian Fest! The lines were long and the weather hot, but worth it for unique food.

name: Celebrity Cupcakes
description: Celebrity Cupcakes, a quaint spot in Houston’s West University near Rice Village, offers an assortment of cupcakes like red velvet and vanilla.
review: Celebrity Cupcakes in Houston’s West University was a letdown. Tucked near Rice Village, these overpriced cupcakes tasted average.

name: Chai Shai
description: Chai Shai, a unique spot in Houston’s Sharpstown on Harwin Drive, serves steaming Kashmiri chai in a no frills setting. Sip Kashmiri chai for a warm treat.
review: Chai Shai in Sharpstown’s ambiance is lacking, set in an old grocery store, but I came for a hot tea and got the Kashmiri chai. It came in a small foam cup but was steaming, fresh, and authentically tasty, loved it!

name: Chang’s Chinese Restaurant
description: Chang’s Chinese Restaurant in Sugar Land is on Highway 6, delivering hearty dishes right to your door.
review: I recently ordered food from Chang’s via Yelp’s Eat 24 app. Had never used the app before and had never ordered food from Chang’s before. I was delighted with Yelp’s delivery service and the taste of my food.

name: Cherrywood Coffeehouse
description: Nestled in Austin’s quirky Cherrywood neighborhood, Cherrywood Coffeehouse on East 38th Street is a vibrant spot for breakfast and coffee lovers.
review: A great place to grab some breakfast in ATX! Love the unique coffeehouse, the patio, and indoor seating. My sister and I grabbed breakfast here for a short while before heading back to HTX. I tried their Cuban con leche..

name: Chez Beignets Quan Ong Tre
description: Chez Beignets Quan Ong Tre in Houston’s Chinatown on Bellaire Boulevard serves hot, fluffy beignets and strong chicory coffee in a bustling, festive atmosphere.
review: Yum! Super crispy and fresh beignets at Chez Beignets in Chinatown! I’m a fan of this busy, lively spot.

name: Chicken Station
description: Savor juicy, charcoal cooked chicken at Chicken Station in Houston’s Magnolia Park, a casual East End spot serving Peruvian style dishes with crispy yucca and sweet plantains.
review: I had a craving for some chicken.. but not any kind of chicken. But a good and juicy one.. that had been marinating for 24 hours and slowly cooking over charcoal. I found what I was looking for here at Chicken Station.

name: Chipotle Mexican Grill
description: A fast casual Mexican spot in Sugar Land known for big, build your own burritos and bowls.
review: Chipotle Mexican Grill in Sugar Land is a Houston area gem for huge burritos! I visit once a year because they’re so filling, stuffed like a newborn baby!

name: Cillie’s Cakes
description: Cillie’s Cakes in Stafford on Murphy Road offers moist cakes with whipped cream frosting and fresh fruit. A Houston area gem for cake lovers.
review: Cillie’s Cakes in Stafford has always been lovely, but their cakes are getting too sweet lately. I’d probably pre order and ask for less sugar next time, as the sweetness drowns out the flavor.

name: Cinnamon’s Bakery
description: Cinnamon’s Bakery, a quaint spot in Sugar Land’s First Colony neighborhood on Highway 6, specializes in warm cinnamon rolls and sticky buns. A delightful stop for Houston area pastry lovers.
review: Cinnamon’s Bakery is a simple, quaint spot in a well known Sugar Land neighborhood. It’s old and a bit outdated inside, but it’s been around forever, and I finally visited recently.

name: Cliff’s Hamburger Grill
description: Travel back in time at Cliff’s Hamburger Grill, a beloved old school burger joint in Houston’s Galleria/Uptown area.
review: Cliff’s Old Fashioned Hamburgers.. where has this place been all my life? I was just here over the past weekend that went by.. & had the opportunity to meet my fellow Yelpers.

name: Cloud 10 Creamery
description: Cloud 10 Creamery, a vibrant spot in Houston’s West University on Rice Boulevard, serves unique flavors like toasted rice and gingersnap sundaes.
review: My 100th review goes to Cloud 10 Creamery in West University! This Houston spot has awesome, eccentric ice cream flavors, perfect for bold dessert lovers.

name: Coco Crepes, Waffles & Coffee
description: Indulge in fluffy crepes at Coco Crepes, Waffles & Coffee in Houston’s Rice Village, a cozy spot on Kirby Drive serving creme brulee crepes and waffles.
review: Coco Crepes in Rice Village is still good, but I wish it were bigger inside. Visited recently on a weekend night with relatives, and we got lucky with the largest table.

name: Coco’s Cafe
description: Coco’s Cafe in Sugar Land, a cozy spot on Highway 6, serves large cups of Taiwanese style milk tea with tapioca.
review: Pretty decent Taiwanese style milk tea with tapioca at Coco’s Cafe in Sugar Land! I didn’t try the food, but the place was packed on a weekend afternoon.

name: Coffee Mill
description: Coffee Mill is one of those charming, blink and you’ll miss it cafés tucked quietly into the bustle of the Galleria area.
review: I like this spot! It's a bit of a hole in the wall. It's super quick to pass by and you can easily miss it. All these years I thought this place only sold coffee beans but it's actually a sit down cafe.

name: Common Bond Bistro & Bakery
description: Common Bond’s Galleria/Uptown location feels like stepping into a soft, pastel washed retreat, warm, open, and effortlessly welcoming.
review: This is such a cozy and lovely location of Common Bond Bistro & Bakery. In fact, this location is probably my favorite within the greater Houston area! It is so open, colorful, warm and inviting with the café.

name: Cornelius Nursery
description: Cornelius Nursery in Sugar Land is a floral escape, bright, lush, expansive, and full of life.
review: What an awesome flower nursery! This spot has it all and more! Its quite a large and extensive flower wonderland, haha.

name: Corner Bakery Cafe
description: Corner Bakery Cafe, a spacious spot in Houston’s West University on Kirby Drive, serves mocha coffee and soup panini combos.
review: Corner Bakery Cafe in Houston’s West University was a delight on a rainy evening! The spacious, dimly lit interior was perfect for relaxing.

name: Cravers’ Corner
description: Cravers’ Corner, a new spot in Sugar Land on Eldridge Road, serves lychee green tea with tapioca and unique ice cream flavors.
review: Cravers’ Corner in Sugar Land, new in November, is a decent Houston area spot for tapioca drinks and ice cream. Craved a tapioca drink, so I got lychee green tea with tapioca.

name: Crescent City Beignets
description: Crescent City Beignets, now on Westheimer Road in Houston, serves classic beignets in a lively plaza. Friendly staff and a vibrant vibe make it great for out of town guests.
review: Glad Crescent City Beignets relocated instead of closing! The new Westheimer spot is in a small, lively plaza, though parking’s tight, I parked at the next plaza over on a busy Friday night.

name: Crescent City Beignets
description: Crescent City Beignets, a charming spot in Houston’s Upper Kirby on Kirby Drive, serves piping hot beignets and cafe au lait.
review: Crescent City Beignets in Houston’s Upper Kirby satisfied my overdue beignet craving! Visited with friends, and the fluffy, sugar dusted fritters arrived hot, beware the steam, I nearly burned my mouth!

name: Croissant-Brioche
description: Croissant Brioche, a cute spot in Houston’s West University on Kirby Drive, serves delectable almond chocolate croissants.
review: Croissant Brioche in West University has the cutest name for a Parisian style bakery in Houston!

name: Cupcake Cafe
description: Cupcake Cafe, a vibrant spot in Sugar Land across from First Colony Mall, serves marble cupcakes and iced coffee in a dreamy, colorful setting.
review: Cupcake Cafe in Sugar Land is a Houston area gem! Finally tried it after lunch at Escalante’s, loved the dreamy design with green, purple, and pink hues, comfy purple couch, and cozy booths.

name: Daiso
description: Get lost in the colorful aisles of Daiso in Houston’s Westchase, a thrifty Japanese store offering ceramic plates, quirky toys, and affordable snacks.
review: Daiso is unlike any other dollar store you walk into.. It’s super colorful and whimsical. This is a thrifty Japanese shop that let’s your imagination run wild. It’s perfect for children, teachers and the creative type.

name: Daiso
description: The Sugar Land Daiso delivers everything shoppers love about this Japanese discount chain, clean design, hyper organized aisles, and an endless spread of charming, practical, and delightfully random finds.
review: Clean, new Daiso shoppe! I’m liking this location in the burbs even more than the original in the city. It’s sparkling clean and super organized, stocked to the brim with quality Japanese products.

name: Dandanah Cafe & Grill
description: Dandanah Cafe & Grill, a rare find in Houston’s Galleria on Westheimer Road, serves hawawshy meat pies and Lavazza café lattes.
review: Dandanah Cafe in Houston’s Galleria is a gem for Mediterranean and rare Egyptian food! My sister and I came for the Egyptian dishes, and I knew what to order.

name: Dandelion Cafe
description: Nestled on Bellaire Boulevard, Dandelion Cafe is a charming Houston area gem that brings cozy vibes and local flavor to the table.
review: I’ve been to Dandelion Cafe twice now and I definitely like the concept of this place. The outside and the inside of the cafe are nicely decorated and inviting.

name: Darband Shishkabob
description: Darband Shishkabob, a no frills spot in Houston’s Sharpstown on Gessner Road, offers quick beef kubideh and hummus for takeout. A Houston gem for Persian food fans.
review: Not sure what happened at Darband Shishkabob in Sharpstown, but the food quality’s gone downhill. My family and I often get takeout here for quick, authentic Persian food, nothing fancy, just standard.

name: Diego’s Cantina
description: Diego’s Cantina, an artistic spot in Sugar Land on Town Center Boulevard, serves vegetarian tamales with roasted corn and mole sauce.
review: Diego’s Cantina in Sugar Land is a Houston area gem, visited twice and loved it! The fresh, light Mexican fare is unique, and the tri colored tortilla chips with salsa are awesome.

name: Ding Tea
description: Ding Tea Sugar Land delivers exactly what you want from a reliable bubble tea stop: consistent drinks, quality tapioca, and a cozy environment tucked into a busy plaza off Highway 6.
review: This is a great choice if you're looking for quality milk tea with tapioca. The environment is warm, creative, and cozy, classic Sugar Land vibes right off Highway 6.

name: Dish Society
description: Dish Society in Houston’s Galleria, a bustling spot on Westheimer Road, serves unique Nutella French toast and skillet potatoes. A Houston brunch favorite.
review: Brunch at Dish Society in the Galleria yesterday wasn’t bad, but not my favorite. My omelette was too flat and crispy with an odd smell, I prefer fluffy, soft eggs and have had better elsewhere.

name: Dolce & Cafe
description: Dolce & Cafe brings a whimsical, European inspired charm to Spring Branch with its cozy interior, spacious seating, and an extensive menu of crepes, brunch favorites, and pastries.
review: Oh gosh, such stiff and awkward service upon stepping into this local cafe. This cafe is quaint and whimsical inside. The interior is quite dark though. The seats are plentiful and decently comfortable. The service?

name: Don Cafe
description: Don Cafe, a shiny new spot in Stafford on Murphy Road, serves vegetarian tofu banh mi and fresh shrimp soft rolls.
review: Don Cafe in Stafford is a Houston area gem for banh mi lovers! So glad to have a spot close to Sugar Land, no need to drive to Midtown! This new cafe is ultra clean and spacious.

name: Double Trouble Caffeine & Cocktails
description: Double Trouble Caffeine & Cocktails, a laid back spot in Houston’s Midtown on Main Street, serves silky coconut cream lattes with beautiful latte art.
review: Double Trouble Caffeine & Cocktails in Midtown Houston was perfect for a quiet Saturday morning. The chill vibe and laid back decor caught my eye, with plenty of indoor and outdoor seating.

name: Droubi’s Bakery & Deli
description: Droubi’s Bakery & Deli, a flavorful spot in Houston on Hillcroft Street, serves juicy chicken shawarma and buttery mamoul pastries.
review: Droubi’s Bakery & Deli in Houston is a gem for chicken shawarma! The juicy, succulent chicken with tangy, garlicky yogurt sauce and slivers of pickles is perfection, I love the tartness!

name: Droubi’s International Imports & Cafe
description: Droubi’s International Imports & Cafe in Sugar Land on Highway 6 was a convenient spot for fresh ingredients and cafe bites, now sadly closed.
review: Droubi’s International Imports & Cafe in Sugar Land was a Houston area gem, but it’s been closed for years, such a shame! As a Sugar Land resident, it was so convenient for Mediterranean ingredients and cafe bites.

name: Dulce Tapioca
description: Dulce Tapioca in Sugar Land serves flavorful juice tea and chewy jumbo pearls in a cozy cafe setting. For Sugar Land bubble tea lovers, the jumbo pearls are a chewy delight, and the juice tea selection is vibrant.
review: Ive been coming to this boba/tapioca/pearl tea spot for quite sometime. Ive even received my tenth free drink after finishing up the deal card. Yay! Though, it took me forever to receive that free drink.
address: 2735 Town Center Blvd N Ste R

name: Dumplings & Noodles by Cooking Girl
description: Dumplings & Noodles by Cooking Girl is a lively destination for noodle lovers and dumpling fans.
review: I wish I could’ve liked the food here but it was just okay. We ordered the fried chicken today as an appetizer and it literally came out as crumbs, almost ‘bottom of the bag’ crumb type.

name: Dunkin'
description: Relive childhood memories at Dunkin’ in Houston’s River Oaks, a clean and quiet spot on West Gray Street. This cozy shop serves devil’s food donuts and complimentary donut holes, perfect for a quick sweet treat.
review: I vaguely remembered Dunkin’ Donuts from childhood on the West Coast, so visiting this River Oaks location was a treat. It was clean and empty on a Saturday afternoon, despite road construction nearby.

name: Dunkin’
description: Dunkin’ in Westchase delivers what it’s best known for: quick, reliable coffee and convenient drive thru service.
review: Dunkin’ serves up some decent hot coffee, always crisp and tasty. Whether hot or iced, it’s a good alternative to the usual Starbucks run.

name: D’amico’s Italian Market Cafe
description: D’amico’s Italian Market Cafe, a rustic spot in Houston’s The Heights on Rice Boulevard, serves potato gnocchi with pesto and warm bread with olive oil.
review: D’amico’s Italian Market Cafe in Houston’s The Heights is a rustic gem in Rice Village! Visited on a busy weekend night, but the prompt service got us seated quickly.

name: Elevation Burger
description: Elevation Burger, a casual spot in Houston’s Upper Kirby on Kirby Drive, serves organic beef burgers and grilled cheese sandwiches.
review: Visited Elevation Burger in Upper Kirby on a quiet Sunday night.

name: Empire Cafe
description: Empire Cafe, a cozy spot in Houston’s Montrose on Westheimer Road, serves standout pasta and decadent cakes.
review: Empire Cafe in Montrose has the best pasta and cake in Houston, hands down! The portions are generous, and the food is simple yet flavorful. Salads and soups are tasty too.

name: Epicure Café
description: Epicure Café, a quaint gem in Houston’s River Oaks on West Gray Street, offers pistachio cake and strong café lattes amid local art displays.
review: Epicure Café in River Oaks is a quaint gem I keep coming back to! The local paintings for sale add such a vibrant touch, popping against the cozy vibe.

name: Fadi’s Mediterranean Grill
description: Fadi’s Mediterranean Grill, a beloved spot in Houston on Westheimer Road, serves fresh Levantine dishes with warm pita bread.
review: Fadi’s Mediterranean Grill in Houston is a Levantine gem! The fresh, warm food has distinct flavors, every dish is amazing! Piled my plate with side dishes yesterday, and each was wonderfully delicious.

name: Fanoosh – Burgers & Biryani
description: Spice up your meal at Fanoosh, Burgers & Biryani in Sugar Land, a Houston area halal spot serving chicken biryani and hearty burgers.
review: I don’t see the hype. I happened to be in the area so I dropped by and ordered two chicken biryani’s to go. The menu selection that’s offered here is quite minimal. Not that many choices.

name: Fellini Caffè
description: Fellini Caffè, an artistic spot in Houston’s West University on Rice Boulevard, serves creamy creme espresso and chef made Italian pastries.
review: Brillante! Fellini Caffè in West University’s Rice Village is a Houston gem! The layout and ambiance are pure art.

name: Fish City Grill
description: Fish City Grill, a cozy spot in Sugar Land on Town Center Boulevard, serves jumbo lump crab cake sandwiches and warm bread pudding.
review: Fish City Grill in Sugar Land was a solid dinner spot with my family. The seafood menu’s small, but everyone enjoyed their meals.

name: FIX Coffeebar
description: FIX Coffeebar is a warm, intimate neighborhood café tucked into Montrose, full of wood textures, glowing bulb lights, and the soft hum of students and creatives typing away.
review: I finally had the chance to try out Fix Coffeebar on a rainy mid week afternoon. Parking is far too few in this part of town, the plaza was packed, and I ended up parking on a corner street, mud everywhere.

name: Flower Child
description: Flower Child in Houston’s Galleria/Uptown is a vibrant spot for healthy, vegetarian friendly meals with a West Coast flair.
review: Portions have drastically decreased at this restaurant… I ordered the mother earth bowl and only had 2 pieces of sweet potato in the bowl.

name: Foam Coffee House
description: Foam Coffee House brings a fun and unexpected pairing to Gulfton: a neighborhood café built right beside a car wash.
review: Liking the concept of Foam Coffee House… your vehicle can get a good scrub a dub dub while you sip on a frothy beverage. A car wash is present within the small lot.

name: Freebirds World Burrito
description: Freebirds World Burrito, a colorful spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, serves fresh vegetarian burritos with a spunky, hippie vibe.
review: Freebirds World Burrito in Sugar Land was a fun first visit! The colorful, hippie vibe with bold walls gave a warm, spunky feel.

name: French Riviera Bakery Cafe
description: French Riviera Bakery Cafe, a charming spot in Houston’s Galleria on Westheimer Road, serves crispy croissants and tuna salad sandwiches.
review: French Riviera Bakery Cafe in Houston’s Galleria was a delightful lunch spot last month! The staff was warm and welcoming, and the food and pastries were delicious.

name: Fresh Boba
description: Satisfy your boba cravings at Fresh Boba, a cozy bubble tea shop in Sugar Land’s Kroger shopping center on University Boulevard.
review: Tried Fresh Boba this evening in the Kroger’s shopping center near Kempner HS in Sugar Land. It wasn’t busy, which was nice.

name: Fresh Dental Care
description: Fresh Dental Care in Houston’s Alief on Bellaire Boulevard offers patient focused service for families and kids.
review: Visited Fresh Dental Care in Alief last Friday as a new patient, and it was packed with families and kids, clearly a go to spot for great dental service!

name: Fresh Off the Bowl
description: Warm up at Fresh Off the Bowl in Houston’s Meyerland, a quiet Vietnamese cafe serving skinny pho and crispy crab wontons. While flavors may vary, it’s a convenient stop for Houstonians seeking a cozy bowl of soup on chilly nights.
review: What the pho? This place wasn’t too good. A friend and I dined here on a chilly Sunday night. It was freezing so we decided upon something warm after having coffee at Fioza. We had no plans on having dinner out..

name: Fruit Frenzy
description: Fruit Frenzy, a colorful spot in Houston’s Galleria on Post Oak Boulevard, serves almond milk tea with firm tapioca pearls.
review: Fruit Frenzy in Houston’s Galleria was a pleasant surprise, I didn’t know it’d been open for months! Visited with my sister in the afternoon when it was quiet, just some students studying.

name: Fruity Yogurt
description: Fruity Yogurt in Sugar Land’s Asian district offers self serve yogurt with fruity toppings like mango and mochi.
review: Ive been wanting to check out this self serve fro ~ yo spot for quite sometime! I love the area that its situated in. The location of this place is considered the Asian district of Sugar Land.

name: Gelato Cup
description: Satisfy your sweet tooth at Gelato Cup in Houston’s Chinatown, a longstanding spot serving pistachio and dark chocolate gelato.
review: Meh. This place was just okay. My dining partner and I walked into this cafe after noticing that Frozen Cafe was closed. & with that in mind, unfortunately, Frozen Cafe will be closed for good soon.

name: George Bush Intercontinental Airport - IAH
description: George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH) in the IAH Airport Area on JFK Boulevard is a major hub, but flight delays and outdated facilities can frustrate.
review: George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH) is the worst! I was stuck for hours due to a delayed flight, then the airline canceled it, how does that make sense?

name: Gigi’s Cupcakes of Sugarland
description: Gigi’s Cupcakes of Sugarland, a vibrant spot on Town Center Boulevard, serves strawberry princess cupcakes and milk chocolate minis.
review: Gigi’s Cupcakes of Sugarland was a fun stop during opening week! Loved the itty bitty milk chocolate cupcake samples with crunchy white pearls, creamy frosting and great texture.

name: Golden Dumpling House
description: Golden Dumpling House is the definition of a hidden gem, small, unassuming, and deeply rooted in the craft of traditional dumpling making.
review: Golden Dumpling House seems to serve up some rather mean, actually, cute and authentic, dumplings. They’re doughy, chewy, and filled to the brim. Inside each dumpling is a hefty meatball like center brimming with flavor.

name: Golem’s Gate
description: Golem’s Gate in Stafford feels like stepping into a pocket sized fantasy realm, warm, welcoming, and brimming with imagination.
review: This is such a neat little mom and pop game store that is tucked in a quiet and cozy little part of town.

name: Got Banh Mi & Pho
description: Savor authentic Vietnamese at Got Banh Mi & Pho, a cozy spot on Westheimer Road in Houston’s Westchase. This vibrant café serves crispy tofu vermicelli bowls and fresh flavors, perfect for a quick, flavorful lunch before work.
review: Finally stopped by Got Banh Mi & Pho on Westheimer before work, and it was as tasty and authentic as I hoped! I’m a huge fan of vermicelli bowls, light, crispy, and never greasy, so I ordered the tofu vermicelli bowl.

name: Grady Park
description: Discover Grady Park, a tranquil urban retreat in Houston’s vibrant Galleria/Uptown area, perfect for families and outdoor enthusiasts.
review: This is a chill, quiet and clean park within the inner loop/galleria area. An urban park situated on Yorktown Drive. A bit of a green nature escape among the concrete plazas of inner loop Houston.

name: Guru Burgers & Bowls
description: Guru Burgers & Bowls, a vibrant spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, serves exotic shaggy crepes and fresh salmon burgers.
review: Guru Burgers & Bowls in Sugar Land is fusion cuisine done right! Visited twice and loved it.

name: Gyro King
description: Gyro King, a bright yellow food truck near Houston’s Medical Center on South Main Street, serves juicy chicken and rice with creamy white sauce.
review: Wow, stellar street food at Gyro King! The New York native owners bring that Big Apple vibe, I felt transported back to NYC’s yellow street carts. Craved chicken and rice with white sauce, and Gyro King delivered!

name: Gyro Republic
description: Gyro Republic brings the classic New York, style chicken and rice experience to the heart of Sugar Land.
review: I’ve visited twice recently, and Gyro Republic is a spot I would’ve overlooked if not for my cousin’s recommendation.

name: H-E-B
description: H E B Sugar Land Market, a massive spot on Highway 6, offers a marvelous cheese display and quality butters, yogurts, and chocolates.
review: H E B Sugar Land Market is a Houston area gem! Visited during opening week, huge and packed! Not quite Central Market, but it offers so much more than regular H E Bs. The lively vibe and friendly staff made it fun.

name: Harvest Express
description: Harvest Express, a vibrant spot across from Houston’s Galleria on Westheimer Road, serves delicious chicken wraps with unlimited toppings and Harvest Sauce.
review: Ate the tastiest, juiciest chicken wrap at Harvest Express near the Galleria! Unlike most places, the chicken wasn’t dry, it tasted like rotisserie and was amazing.

name: Harvest Organic Grille
description: Harvest Organic Grille, a rustic spot in Houston’s Galleria on Post Oak Boulevard, serves vegan red lentil patties and green detox juice.
review: Harvest Organic Grille in Houston’s Galleria is awesome for organic, vegan, and gluten free options, perfect for any diner! The rustic, warm interior is lovely, especially for winter meals.

name: Haute Pets Mobile Grooming Salon
description: Treat your furry friend to Haute Pets Mobile Grooming Salon, a premium service based in Houston’s Fourth Ward that travels to suburbs like Sugar Land.
review: Haute Pets Mobile Grooming Salon offers great service! Perfect for my spoiled Himalayan cat who deserves the best care.

name: Hippo Ice
description: Discover a unique dessert at Hippo Ice, a charming spot in a quiet Sugar Land neighborhood on New Territory Boulevard. Their creamy coconut shaved ice with fruit and mango puree is perfect for a late night treat.
review: Hippo Ice in Sugar Land, open just over a year, is tucked in a quiet neighborhood, and I finally tried it a few days ago. It was my first time having shaved ice, and I love the concept!

name: Honey Bee Teahouse & Fast Food
description: Honey Bee Teahouse & Fast Food, a hidden gem in Houston’s Chinatown on Bellaire Boulevard, serves cold, satisfying milk tea in playful cups.
review: Visited Honey Bee Teahouse in Houston’s Chinatown a few weeks ago, bit tricky to find with all the construction around! I was craving milk tea, and reviews said it’s good here.

name: House of Bowls
description: Savor authentic Hong Kong style cuisine at House of Bowls in Houston’s Chinatown, a cozy spot on Bellaire Boulevard serving creamy shrimp chow fun, curry Singaporean noodles, and eggy French toast.
review: Nam nam nam! House of Bowls serves true Hong Kong style food, totally different from typical Chinese fare with its own flair. Great spot for something unique in Chinatown. I love visiting on quiet weekend nights.

name: Houston Italian Festival
description: Experience Houston’s cultural scene at the Houston Italian Festival in Montrose, a long running event celebrating Italian heritage with food, music, and vendors.
review: Oh gosh. This festival was awful. Should I have read the reviews? Sure. But viewing the Yelp rating on this fest didn’t come to mind. I was on a mission to enjoy a festival thats been well known in the city of Houston.

name: Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo
description: Saddle up for the Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo in the Medical Center, a iconic Houston event with petting zoos, carnival rides, and boutique shopping.
review: It was my first time ever visiting the Rodeo. I knew it really wasn’t my thing and boy was I correct. My friends and I visited over the weekend on a Sunday afternoon. It happened to be a cool and cloudy day. Thankfully.

name: Houston Marriott Sugar Land
description: Houston Marriott Sugar Land, a pristine hotel on Town Center Boulevard, offers a clean front hall and courtyard for lounging.
review: Houston Marriott Sugar Land is a Houston area gem! I haven’t stayed here, but my friends and I love hanging out in the clean, organized front hall and courtyard, no issues ever!

name: HTeaO
description: Quench your thirst at HTeaO in Sugar Land serving a vibrant array of Southern style iced teas, from minty black tea to the Ryan Palmer lemonade blend.
review: HTeaO on the go! This cool little spot has a large variety of chilled teas. Simple & classic Southern style teas ranging from fruit flavors, as well as plain dark and deep black tea flavors (sweet regular).

name: Ichiban Sushi & Tapioca
description: Ichiban Sushi & Tapioca in Sugar Land offers Japanese dishes, tapioca drinks, and new ice cream treats. A promising spot for ice cream treats.
review: The tapioca here is horrible! The pearls are very hard, and not chewable. I shouldve came back and replaced it for another non ~ pearl drink. I may try out the Japanese food next door. Though, ive heard that its decent.

name: Imperial Farmers Market
description: Discover fresh, local goods at Imperial Farmers Market in Sugar Land, a vibrant market on Highway 6 with baked goods, fresh produce, and handmade jewelry.
review: Imperial Farmers Market is right in my Sugar Land neighborhood, but I hadn’t visited in years until last weekend. It’s grown so much!

name: In-N-Out Burger
description: In N Out Burger remains one of those rare fast food spots where simplicity truly shines, and the Stafford location captures that charm perfectly.
review: This is such a great location of In and Out. Fast service and friendly folks just waiting to take your order. Menu is quite simple and easy. Food is always fresh and stellar at this location.

name: Inside Scoop Frozen Custard & Yogurt
description: Inside Scoop Frozen Custard & Yogurt, a family owned spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, serves creamy vanilla frozen custard with toppings like almonds.
review: Inside Scoop Frozen Custard & Yogurt in Sugar Land was a dream come true for my first frozen custard try! This family owned Houston area spot has amazing customer service, warm and welcoming.

name: Inversion Coffee House
description: Inversion Coffee House, a laid back spot in Houston’s Montrose on Montrose Boulevard, serves silky café lattes amid colorful art.
review: Inversion Coffee House in Montrose is a nice Houston spot with ample parking and colorful art on the walls. Visited on a Sunday night, and it wasn’t too crowded. The menu’s simple, no overwhelming choices, which I liked.

name: Jambeto’s Bakery & Cafe
description: Jambeto’s Bakery & Cafe, a quaint spot in Stafford on Dulles Avenue, serves mini bundt cakes and Halo Halo drinks.
review: Jambeto’s Bakery & Cafe in Stafford is a new, quaint Filipino spot near Houston. They’ve got mini bundt cakes, sheet cakes, and savory Filipino foods.

name: Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ
description: Tucked inside the bustling HMart food court, this express version of Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ offers a slimmed down menu compared to the full service locations in Bellaire and Sugar Land.
review: This seems to be an express version of Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ, tucked inside the newer HMart in Katy. Having visited the Bellaire and Sugar Land locations, I’ve always liked their food and menu options.

name: Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ
description: Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ has long been a dependable Sugar Land spot for hearty Korean comfort food, piping hot tofu soups, sizzling bulgogi, and a spread of banchan to round out the experience.
review: Decent food, terrible service. I've been dining here for years and the menu has gone through a few changes. I used to love their kimchi dumplings that were made purely out of kimchi and nothing else.

name: Java Pura Coffee Roasters
description: Tucked inside a row of unassuming office style buildings near Chimney Rock, Java Pura is one of Houston’s most meaningful hidden gems. This isn’t a café, it’s a working roastery, a coffee lab, and a hub for true bean obsessives.
review: A gem of a coffee roaster headquartered in Gulfton, near Chimney Rock. It’s a bit difficult to find, just a row of plain office buildings, but that adds to the adventure of locating this coffee lab.

name: JL Foot Spa
description: Unwind at JL Foot Spa, a cozy upstairs retreat in Houston’s Chinatown plaza on Bellaire Boulevard. This budget friendly spot offers a one hour foot and body massage for just $20, complete with complimentary green tea.
review: Nice little foot spa at JL Foot Spa, upstairs in a big, well lit Chinatown plaza. Visited with family, and we all got the basic foot massage, which turned into a full hour body massage too, such a steal at $20!

name: Juicy Box
description: A Taiwanese dessert and juice bar in Chinatown serving shaved snow, fruit bowls, and cool, refreshing treats.
review: Juicy Box in Chinatown is a nice spot for a frozen treat that’s a bit different! Got the mixed fruit bowl with coconut and strawberry ice cream, asked for an extra scoop, and they paired so well!

name: Jusgo Supermarket
description: Jusgo Supermarket is a spacious, bright, and somewhat mysterious international market, equal parts grocery store and small business gallery.
review: All is determination, To make it make sense All is determination, You can find it if you ## Just let go, just let go, just, let it go ~ Fischerspooner A nice, large, bright supermarket, expansive yet a bit desolate.

name: Jus’ Mac Sugar Land
description: Jus’ Mac Sugar Land, a cozy spot on University Boulevard, serves creamy popeye mac and cheese with spinach and mushrooms.
review: Jus’ Mac in Sugar Land is a Houston area gem! Knew their Heights location, but this one’s in my neighborhood now. Visited with a friend and loved the cute, urban vibe.

name: Kabob Cafe
description: Kabob Cafe, a quick stop spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, serves convenient kabobs with Sunday lunch specials. Try a kabob plate for a savory bite.
review: Kabob Cafe in Sugar Land is a decent Houston area spot for quick Persian food. The food is good but not mind blowing, no wow factor, but it’s fast and convenient if you’re craving kabobs.

name: Kabob Korner
description: Kabob Korner, a bustling spot in Houston on Hillcroft Avenue, serves chicken shawarma and Pakistani chai.
review: Kabob Korner in Houston was bustling at lunchtime, and I regret not trying the Pakistani dishes everyone raved about! I was mall bound, so I wanted a filling meal.

name: Kamalan Bakery
description: Discover soft, airy breads at Kamalan Bakery in Houston’s Chinatown, a clean and organized spot on Bellaire Boulevard.
review: Super soft and fluffy breads at Kamalan Bakery in Chinatown! Visited on a Sunday evening, and there were still some items available, love their late hours for a convenient walk in.

name: Keeper’s Japanese Restaurant & Bar
description: Keeper’s Japanese Restaurant & Bar, a modern spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, offers a large sushi menu and crispy shrimp eggrolls.
review: Keeper’s Japanese Restaurant in Sugar Land has a large sushi menu and a modern, spacious feel that I liked right away.

name: Koffeteria
description: Koffeteria brings an artistic, vintage charm to EaDo, a neighborhood known for its creative energy and urban edge.
review: Unique and vintage coffee shoppe within the EaDo district of Houston. This part of town isn't too far off from the novelty of hanging out, or heading towards downtown htx.

name: Kolache Shoppe – Greenway
description: Kolache Shoppe in Greenway is the definition of a warm, comforting morning stop, tucked quietly into a cozy corner of Houston’s inner loop.
review: Tucked in a cozy corner on Greenway… Kolache Shoppe is a nice option for a quick and warm breakfast experience. They close at 12pm, so get there before then! Plenty of vegetarian and meat options like brisket kolaches.

name: Kona Grill
description: Kona Grill in Sugar Land offers vegetarian sushi and margherita pizza in a casual dining setting.
review: I came here last summer for my sisters birthday party get together. The service was not so great, considering we had a huge group of people. My sister and I shared the margherita pizza. It was absolutely horrible!

name: Koryo Bakery
description: Koryo Bakery in Houston’s Memorial on Gessner Road offers mini cakes, breads, and almond cakes. A local Houston spot for pastry enthusiasts.
review: Koryo Bakery in Memorial had a strong, strange smell when I walked in, not the cozy vanilla or butter vibe I expected.

name: Kublai Khan Stir-Fry
description: Kublai Khan Stir Fry, a unique spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, offers a Mongolian grill experience with fresh meats and produce.
review: Kublai Khan Stir Fry in Sugar Land was my first try at a Mongolian grill, but I’m not sure I’ll be back. Not sure how long the meats and produce sit out, but I had a terrible stomach ache the next day.

name: Kung Fu Tea
description: Satisfy your boba cravings at Kung Fu Tea in Houston’s Chinatown, a lively spot on Bellaire Boulevard serving frothy iced milk tea with perfect tapioca pearls.
review: Nice experience at Kung Fu Tea on a busy Saturday night! Went with friends, and surprisingly, the line wasn’t too long, quick and efficient. My go to is iced milk tea with tapioca, perfect for Houston’s heat.

name: La Argentina Gelato & Coffee
description: La Argentina Gelato & Coffee is a small, tucked away spot offering South American, style gelato and baked treats. While its reputation has generated quite a bit of buzz, this particular visit left room for improvement.
review: I thought this spot was just alright. What a hype. Location wise, it is not the easiest to spot, tucked away in a corner of an area that is typically not frequented. In regards to customer service?

name: La Baguette French Bakery
description: La Baguette French Bakery, a quirky spot in Houston’s Midtown on Gray Street, serves tasty vegetarian banh mi with crispy French bread.
review: Popped into La Baguette French Bakery in Midtown Houston on a freezing Saturday at 10:45 a.m. Other cafes were closed, so I tried this spot. First time here, and the dark lit vibe and priceless menu were odd.

name: LA Crawfish
description: LA Crawfish in Memorial brings a lively blend of Cajun heat and Vietnamese comfort food to one tucked away corner inside 99 Ranch Market.
review: LA Crawfish, no, not Los Angeles, y’all. This is all about Louisiana style grub. The food here is coated with spice and heavy handed with salt and oil, but that’s typically the palate of Cajun/crawfish cuisine.

name: La La Land Kind Café
description: La La Land Kind Café brings all the dreamy, feel good charm, white picket fence, golden sunlight, cozy porch seating, and a whimsical interior that looks straight out of a movie set.
review: I feel like I’ve stepped into a movie set walking into this place, white picket fence, cozy porch, and a polished, ultra preppy interior.

name: La Super Hueva Tacos y Tortas
description: Satisfy late night cravings at La Super Hueva Tacos y Tortas in Houston’s Westchase, a vibrant taco truck serving beef and barbacoa tacos with zesty green salsa.
review: Wait. What? I just noticed this taco truck changed their name as I’m sitting here writing this review. This place has some decent late night grub.

name: Lamppost Coffee
description: Lamppost Coffee brings soft minimalism, clean design, and a warm welcome to the Austin café scene.
review: I adore the minimal, clean, yet simple aesthetic of this coffee shoppe! The name is just as charming. The folks running the shop are friendly and can whip up any beverage to your liking.

name: Lava Coffee
description: With its industrial, European blend of décor, glowing ambient bulbs, and plush seating, this Katy hideaway feels both stylish and comforting.
review: I’m loving the warm industrial meets European décor here, soft lights, cozy chairs, and a posh vibe tucked quietly within Katy Asia Town.

name: Les Givral's Sandwich & Café
description: Les Givral's Sandwich & Café, a bustling spot in Houston’s Midtown on Travis Street, serves aromatic shrimp fried rice and soft shrimp rolls.
review: Finally made it to Les Givral’s in Midtown Houston, and it was worth the wait! Tucked in a cute corner, this spot outshines the okay ish cafes nearby.

name: LN Beauty Express
description: Get a fresh trim at LN Beauty Express, a popular hair salon in Sugar Land’s First Colony on Sweetwater Boulevard. Book a trim with plenty of time.
review: Got to LN Beauty Express in Sugar Land at 11:30 for my appointment, but waited 15 minutes and counting because my usual hairstylist was still with another client.

name: Local Foods
description: Local Foods in Houston’s West University on Kirby Drive offers unique sandwiches on freshly baked bread, vegan sides, and fresh seafood.
review: Almost all the sandwiches at Local Foods are delicious and unique! I’ve tried most and I’m a fan. The freshly baked breads are crunchy and tasty, making every sandwich special.

name: Lopez Mexican Restaurant
description: Lopez Mexican Restaurant, a spacious spot in Houston on Wilcrest Drive, serves shrimp fajitas with classic beans and rice.
review: Lopez Mexican Restaurant in Houston was just okay, nothing spectacular. I ordered the shrimp fajitas, but they were rubbery and overcooked, not great.

name: Luce Ave Coffee Roasters
description: Discover Luce Ave Coffee Roasters, a minimalist haven in Houston’s Greenway area, where coffee is an art form.
review: Minimal.. clean.. sleek atmosphere. I had the chance to visit Luce Ave Coffee Roasters last month with a friend. This little coffee shop is centrally located within the inner loop and makes for a nice place to hangout.

name: Luna Pizzeria
description: Luna Pizzeria, a stellar spot in Houston’s Upper Kirby on Kirby Drive, serves delicious mushroom and vegetarian pies.
review: Luna Pizzeria in Upper Kirby is such a stellar spot for satisfying pizza! I don’t eat pizza often, but when I’m craving a cheesy slice, this place is my go to.

name: L’Occitane En Provence
description: Explore luxurious skincare at L’Occitane En Provence in Houston’s Galleria, a chic boutique on Westheimer Road offering premium beauty products.
review: My review of L’Occitane in the Galleria is all about customer service, which matters a lot to me. My friends and I walked in this afternoon, and the older woman at the register didn’t greet us, look our way, or smile.

name: M&M Grill
description: M&M Grill, a casual spot in Houston’s Medical Center on Fannin Street, serves moist chicken soft tacos and cheesy enchiladas.
review: M&M Grill in Houston’s Medical Center is a family favorite! This shabby chic hole in the wall has limited seating and red walls, giving Rockets basketball vibes, kids were even watching a game!

name: Maggie Moo’s Ice Cream & Treatery
description: Maggie Moo’s Ice Cream & Treatery, a colorful spot in Sugar Land on Town Center Boulevard, serves unique, scrumptious ice cream flavors. Try a unique flavor for a creamy bite.
review: Maggie Moo’s in Sugar Land is a Houston area classic! This colorful, cute ice cream parlor has been here forever, a true Sugar Land staple. I remember coming as a kid, and the unique, scrumptious flavors still impress.

name: Magic Cup
description: Beat the Houston heat at Magic Cup in Alief, a clean and spacious café on Bellaire Boulevard serving creamy milk tea, smoothies, and fresh fruit juices.
review: Super crisp and creamy milk tea at Magic Cup! Stopped by today after spotting this new café on my drive to the dentist. It was such a hot day, and I needed a cold, refreshing drink.

name: Magnol French Baking
description: Magnol French Baking is one of Houston’s most delightful hidden gems, a true Parisian inspired treasure tucked inside an industrial pocket of Spring Branch.
review: Incredibly tasty, very buttery and authentically French. Magnol Bakery is a true hole in the wall spot. This spot is located within a discrete and rather industrial part of town.

name: Mai Colachi
description: Savor authentic Pakistani cuisine at Mai Colachi, an elegant restaurant in a convenient Sugar Land plaza on Highway 6. This vibrant spot serves flavorful dishes, fluffy breads, and passion fruit drinks, perfect for a family dinner.
review: Mai Colachi in Sugar Land serves authentic, flavorful Pakistani cuisine in an elegant setting, the ambiance totally matches the vibe!

name: Maiberry
description: Maiberry, a vibrant spot in Sugar Land’s First Colony Mall, serves creamy yogurt with natural ingredients and cane sugar.
review: Maiberry in Sugar Land’s First Colony Mall is a refreshing Houston area gem! Love their natural ingredients and pure cane sugar, creamy yogurt keeps me full while shopping. It’s a healthy mall option!

name: Mama Yu
description: Mama Yu, a family run spot in Houston’s Alief on Dairy Ashford Road, serves flavorful chicken satay and fragrant nasi goreng.
review: Mama Yu in Houston’s Alief serves tasty Indonesian food! Every dish has a unique, flavorful appeal, not too spicy.

name: Marble Slab Creamery
description: Tucked into a busy Stafford shopping plaza, this long standing Marble Slab Creamery offers a simple, familiar stop for classic scoops and mix ins.
review: I hadn’t visited this location in years. It’s tucked into a large shopping plaza in a busy part of Stafford, one I used to frequent over a decade ago when this was a Cold Stone Creamery. This Marble Slab is just OK.

name: Marco’s Pizza
description: Marco’s Pizza, a convenient spot in Sugar Land on Eldridge Road, delivers hot white cheesy pizza and cheesy bread.
review: Marco’s Pizza in Sugar Land is a decent neighborhood joint, just minutes from my place.

name: Maria Yari Salon
description: Maria Yari Salon is one of Sugar Land’s quietly legendary beauty stops, small, personal, and fully driven by the skill of one expert: Maria herself.
review: I've been gettin' my brows threaded by Maria for well over a decade. Much before she opened up her own salon. Been chasin' her around cause she's really the only one who can touch my face.

name: Market Place Antiques & Collectibles
description: Market Place Antiques & Collectibles is a sprawling, delightfully dusty treasure hunt tucked into Spring Branch, a warehouse style maze of booths, vendors, and relics from eras long gone.
review: Decent and quite a large marketplace to explore on a random weekend afternoon.

name: Masala Munchies
description: Masala Munchies, a grab and go spot in Houston’s Sharpstown on Harwin Drive, serves punchy potato samosas and chaat.
review: Masala Munchies in Sharpstown has the best potato samosas! They’re smaller than others in Houston, but I prefer that, they’re packed with flavor and don’t leave you stuffed.

name: Mazajj Organic Coffee
description: Step into Mazajj Organic Coffee in Houston’s Galleria/Uptown for a cozy escape filled with authentic chai and warm vibes.
review: Absolutely wonderful interior, lots of indoor lighting as well as natural lighting pouring in through the windows. Great customer service and warm hospitality, thanks guys!

name: McAlister’s Deli
description: McAlister’s Deli, a convenient spot in Houston’s Third Ward on a university campus, serves vegetarian bean chili and creamy mac and cheese.
review: McAlister’s Deli in Houston’s Third Ward is a campus gem! This one stop deli serves sandwiches, soups, and salads, perfect for a hungry student. The vegetarian bean chili was decent and filling, great for an empty belly.

name: Menchie’s Frozen Yogurt
description: Menchie’s Frozen Yogurt, a self serve spot in Sugar Land on University Boulevard, offers a variety of yogurt flavors and mix ins. Try a custom yogurt mix for a sweet bite.
review: Menchie’s Frozen Yogurt in Sugar Land didn’t live up to the hype. Excited for a new yogurt spot, I found the self serve layout odd, yogurt bar behind the counter made it cramped with people sampling.

name: Mercantile
description: Savor a smooth iced vanilla latte at Mercantile, a charming coffee shop in Houston’s West University on Kirby Drive.
review: Mercantile in West University has one of the best coffee selections in Rice Village, way better than Starbucks! I’d stopped by before to browse their shelves but finally got an iced vanilla latte on a hot afternoon.

name: Milk Mustache
description: Step into the sugary charm of Milk Mustache, a whimsical cookie shop tucked into Fountain View in the Galleria/Uptown area. This isn’t your average dessert spot, it’s a full sensory experience.
review: Yummy cookies galore. Milk Mustache honestly has some of the best cookies in the city. They are warm, crispy and yet gooey as well. Classic texture and flavor. It’s cute and whimsical inside.

name: Minuti Coffee
description: Step into Minuti Coffee in Houston’s bustling Galleria/Uptown area for a warm, Italian inspired coffee experience that feels like a mini vacation.
review: Warm and glowing aesthetics within a clean environment. I like this small and cozy Minuti coffee house. There’s plenty of seating within the café, even with the limited space.

name: Minuti Coffee
description: Transport yourself to Italy at Minuti Coffee, a Sugar Land coffee haven serving rich ciocco de leche and bold Modena imported brews.
review: I love the masculine, Italian feel of this coffeehouse. I feel as if, suddenly I have been transported to Italia.

name: Mission Burrito
description: Mission Burrito, a casual spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, serves customizable burritos with spinach tortillas and grilled shrimp.
review: Mission Burrito in Sugar Land is a Houston area gem! Back after a year, I chose a spinach tortilla burrito with cilantro rice, shrimp, beans, veggies, sour cream, and guacamole, huge and satisfying!

name: Mochinut Houston Heights
description: Mochinut Houston Heights delivers exactly what mochi donut lovers crave, warm, crispy exteriors, soft chewy centers, and flavor combinations that keep every visit exciting.
review: Pretty good. Warm, crispy yet chewy at the same time. A mochi donut should have that distinct chewiness. This location serves up some good products. Everything is fresh and customer service is great.

name: Monster Dessert Bar
description: Monster Dessert Bar, a brand new spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, serves creamy cake batter frozen yogurt and vanilla cupcakes.
review: Monster Dessert Bar in Sugar Land is brand spankin’ new! Visited two weeks ago with a friend, and it still had that fresh ‘open sign’ vibe. The layout is neat and clean with small tables.

name: Moxies
description: Dive into the vibrant scene at Moxies, a Galleria/Uptown hotspot that pulses with energy in Houston’s nightlife.
review: Too much party scene. So little substance. Came here on a Friday night. There’s a certain ‘image’ this place tries to maintain. It was crowded. No where to sit. Wasn’t greeted upon entering. Felt the same way upstairs.

name: Mr. Wish
description: Fresh, juicy, bright, and made with real ingredients, Mr. Wish offers a refreshing break from the heavy, creamer based milk teas found at many shops.
review: They say dairy does the body good. But I'm not too sure about that. Sometimes over doing it with milk tea leaves ya' belly bloated and hankering for something lighter. Most of these milk teas are questionable as well.

name: MTea & Coffee
description: Cool off at MTea & Coffee in Sugar Land, a cozy Houston area cafe on Highway Six serving fresh watermelon juice and sea salt foam green tea.
review: MTea & Coffee is yet another new and cozy cafe thats popped up in Sugar Land. Its visibly noticeable and tucked on Highway Six.. although they haven’t put up an official sign as of yet.

name: Naha Thai Restaurant
description: Naha Thai Restaurant brings warmth, flavor, and genuine hospitality to Sugar Land’s dining scene.
review: 111th review! :) Naha Thai is fantastic..! From the food, to the environment, as well as the service.. there isn't much to say except that it's warm and cozy.

name: Nails by Yen
description: Nails by Yen has evolved over the years into a reliably warm, clean, and friendly neighborhood salon.
review: Great service, it has improved over the years. Many of the nail technicians are friendly and will remember you if you visit often. Joanne and Audrey are always friendly and socialize with everyone.

name: Naseeb Indian Restaurant
description: Naseeb Indian Restaurant, a welcoming spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, offers a steaming buffet with diverse dishes and hot milk tea.
review: Not usually a buffet fan, but Naseeb Indian Restaurant in Sugar Land won me over! Visited with my sister and mom on a Friday afternoon, and the staff greeted us kindly.

name: Nazif’s
description: Nazif’s, an authentic spot in Houston on Westheimer Road, serves crunchy kibbi and creamy rice pudding with Turkish tea.
review: Nazif’s in Houston cooks authentic Turkish food, fresh from my recent Turkiye trip! Visited on a quiet weekend afternoon with family, and we got prompt, kind service.

name: Nikoz Fusion Grill
description: Nikoz Fusion Grill, a spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, serves grilled beef souvlaki with hummus and salads.
review: Nikoz Fusion Grill in Sugar Land is hit or miss. Many menu items weren’t available, which was a letdown. I ordered beef souvlaki with a side salad and hummus. The grilled beef was nicely flavored and the only highlight.

name: Nom Mi Street
description: Nom Mi Street, a colorful food truck in Houston’s MacGregor near the University of Houston, serves toasty vegetarian banh mi and fusion fries.
review: Nom Mi Street in Houston’s MacGregor is the cutest, most colorful food truck! Got a vegetarian banh mi with fried tofu, veggies, and cilantro, toasty and flavorful, though the tofu was a bit too fried for me.

name: Nordstrom Ebar Artisan Coffee
description: Savor a fragrant honey almond latte at Nordstrom Ebar Artisan Coffee, a cozy spot in Houston’s Galleria on Westheimer Road. A delightful pick me up for Houston coffee lovers.
review: Nordstrom Ebar Artisan Coffee in the Galleria always delivers great coffee! It’s my favorite spot for a warm, comforting latte during a shopping stroll.

name: Nordstrom Houston Galleria E-Bar
description: Nordstrom Houston Galleria’s E Bar, a cozy coffee nook downstairs in the Galleria, serves honey almond lattes and iced peach tea.
review: Nordstrom’s E Bar in Houston’s Galleria is a hidden gem, not the clothing store! Tucked downstairs, this coffee spot is a delight. The honey almond latte is one of the best coffees I’ve had, beautifully flavored!

name: Nothing Bundt Cakes
description: Nothing Bundt Cakes, a beloved spot in Sugar Land on Town Center Boulevard, serves velvety red velvet bundt cakes with tangy cream cheese frosting.
review: Haven’t been inside Nothing Bundt Cakes in Sugar Land, but their treats at events are amazing! Tried the red velvet bundt cake, so moist with a true velvety texture, unlike most.

name: Old Saigon Cafe
description: Step into the magic of Old Saigon Cafe, a hidden gem on Houston’s Westheimer Road that serves up vibrant Vietnamese flavors.
review: Dining here was magical. The food tasted amazing and it was a special night overall. Appreciated the warm service and hospitality. The menu displays a variety of items to nosh on.

name: Orange Nail Spa & Facial
description: Pamper yourself at Orange Nail Spa & Facial, a lovely spot in a convenient Sugar Land plaza on University Boulevard.
review: Such a lovely nail spa at Orange Nail Spa & Facial, tucked in a convenient Sugar Land plaza! It’s right down the street from me, but my first visit was amazing. Tony greeted me warmly and said I’d be helped soon.

name: Paciugo Gelato
description: Paciugo Gelato, a vibrant spot in Sugar Land on Town Center Boulevard, serves low fat panna cotta and chocolate sorbetti.
