review: Paciugo Gelato in Sugar Land is a Houston area gem! Authentic, fresh flavors like panna cotta, chocolate sorbetti, and berry gelato are low fat and guilt free. The small cup is stuffed generously, perfectly satisfying!

name: Paciugo Gelato & Caffè
description: Indulge in a scoop of gelato at Paciugo Gelato & Caffè in Houston’s West University, nestled in a bustling plaza on Kirby Drive. A lively spot for Houston dessert lovers.
review: Paciugo in West University has a huge selection of gelato and coffee drinks, with lots of holiday beverages when I visited. But the gelato was way too sweet, I could barely finish my small cup.

name: Pangea Bar & Grill
description: Transport yourself to a sultan’s palace at Pangea Bar & Grill, a glowing Mediterranean gem in Houston’s Gulfton neighborhood.
review: I recently visited Pangea with my sister and a good friend of ours. We came here on the night of New Year’s Eve. The outside of the restaurant was vividly glowing at night. The inside was lit up as well.

name: Paper Co Cafe
description: Paper Co Cafe, an airy spot in Houston’s Sixth Ward on Washington Avenue, serves smooth iced vanilla lattes in an industrial setting.
review: Stepped into Paper Co Cafe in the Sixth Ward on a sweltering Saturday after Asian Fest, and the industrial, airy vibe was a relief! It was busy with church members hosting an event, but most folks were friendly.

name: Pappa Geno’s
description: Crave a hefty sandwich at Pappa Geno’s in Houston’s Montrose, a bright, late night spot serving Philly cheesesteaks and crispy fries.
review: I tried out Papa Geno’s late last night. This newly opened sandwich business is tucked in a dimly lit plaza. Within the trenches of Montrose. It’s quite clean and bright inside. But I had an awful experience.

name: Path Of Tea
description: Unwind at Path Of Tea in Houston’s Upper Kirby neighborhood, a lovely tea shop on Kirby Drive offering fruity yummy bear tea and mini hazelnut cakes.
review: Lovely little tea shop at Path Of Tea in Upper Kirby! Wanted to try it for a while and visited after a Trader Joe’s trip.

name: Pho Ben
description: Savor crisp, flavorful Vietnamese cuisine at Pho Ben, a cozy spot in Sugar Land on University Boulevard. This local favorite serves generous portions of pho, banh mi, and rice noodle bowls, all packed with fresh herbs and veggies.
review: Always tasty Vietnamese food at Pho Ben! It’s literally in my Sugar Land neighborhood, and I should visit more since it’s convenient, clean, and has light, fresh food.

name: Pho Saigon
description: Pho Saigon, a well known spot in Houston’s Spring Branch on Long Point Road, serves crispy tofu banh mi and noodle bowls.
review: Something about Pho Saigon in Spring Branch was off putting. I was in the area and knew it’s a well known Houston spot with multiple locations, so I gave it a try. First visit, and I’m not sure I’ll be back.

name: Phoenicia Specialty Foods
description: Phoenicia Specialty Foods, a vibrant market in Houston’s Westchase on Westheimer Road, offers fresh pita bread and kanafeh desserts.
review: Phoenicia Specialty Foods in Houston’s Westchase is a foodie gem! This ethnic market is a treasure trove for cooking, unique produce, meats, and dry goods.

name: Piccomolo Italian Ice Cream
description: Piccomolo Italian Ice Cream, a sweet spot in Sugar Land near Half Price Books, serves generous sorbetti and creamy gelato.
review: Piccomolo Italian Ice Cream in Sugar Land is a Houston area gem! Not my top gelato spot, but I love having it nearby.

name: Pizza 101
description: Pizza 101 in Sugar Land on Highway 6 offers bold flavors like chicken tikka and kebab pizzas, perfect for adventurous eaters. This casual spot serves generous portions with thick crusts, ideal for feeding a crowd.
review: Good pizza at Pizza 101, but not the best I’ve had. They offer unique choices like chicken tikka and kebab pizzas, which caught me off guard with the cheddar cheese, used to mozzarella or ricotta on my pies.

name: PJ’s Coffee
description: PJ’s Coffee in Pearland brings a taste of New Orleans, style brewing to the Houston suburbs, offering distinctive iced drinks, fresh beignets, and a warm café atmosphere.
review: I like this little spot! I really do. My biggest gripe is the air ventilation and all the house flies swarming around the cafe. It literally smells like old oil in here and the ventilation is not the best.

name: Proud Pie
description: Indulge in sweet, homemade pies at Proud Pie, a Katy gem with a food truck stationed in Sugar Land and a shop on Grand Parkway.
review: Finally got to try Proud Pie over the weekend at their food truck in Sugar Land! The actual shop is a bit far, so I was thrilled to catch them near the Museum of Natural Science.

name: Pueblo Viejo
description: Pueblo Viejo in Austin’s Oltorf/East Riverside area is a shabby chic food truck that serves up supreme tacos worth visiting twice in one day.
review: Supreme tacos! Oh my! These tacos tickled my tastebuds in delight and left me wanting for more. My sister and I ended up @ Pueblo Viejo twice in one day. We arrived to Austin early for lunch..

name: Purple Vanilla Frozen Yogurt And Ice Cream
description: Purple Vanilla Frozen Yogurt And Ice Cream, a cozy spot in Houston’s West University on Rice Boulevard, serves soft serve white chocolate frozen yogurt with generous toppings.
review: Purple Vanilla Frozen Yogurt And Ice Cream in West University whips up decent soft serve yogurt! I tried the white chocolate flavor, a bit too sweet for me, but still enjoyable.

name: Pythagoras Conscious Food Philosophy
description: Discover a mindful dining experience at Pythagoras Conscious Food Philosophy, a cozy vegan café tucked in Sugar Creek plaza, Sugar Land.
review: Such a cozy little spot! I’m liking this conscious food philosophy on a quiet yet nonchalant corner of Sugar Creek plaza.

name: Ramen Bar Ichi
description: Dive into Japanese flavors at Ramen Bar Ichi in Houston’s Westchase, an izakaya style spot serving ponzu fried chicken and cold ramen noodle salads.
review: I’m not the biggest fan of ramen.. and it being highly glutinous in nature.. I try to stay away from it. My preference would lean towards rice noodles over wheat based noodles.

name: Randalls
description: Randalls on Hwy 6 is one of Sugar Land’s longstanding neighborhood staples, familiar, comfortable, and refreshingly manageable in size.
review: This Randalls has been around my neighborhood forever. Conveniently located on Hwy 6, it’s gotten a facelift over the years, though walking inside still feels nostalgic, like stepping back in time.

name: Red Circle Ice Cream
description: Treat yourself at Red Circle Ice Cream in Houston’s Chinatown, a trendy spot serving creamy soft serve with crispy churros and bubble waffles.
review: I came here one week ago with my friends after having dinner in the area. It’s nice to finally have this dessert concept in Houston. There are plenty of ice cream shops with the same concept in Los Angeles.

name: Red Dessert Dive
description: Red Dessert Dive, a charming spot in Houston’s The Heights on Studewood Street, serves mouthwatering chocolate chip cookies and brownies made with Valrhona chocolate.
review: Red Dessert Dive in The Heights has such mouthwatering, unique desserts! I wish it was closer, but maybe that’s good for my sweet tooth.

name: Red Mango
description: Red Mango, a bustling spot in Houston’s West University in Rice Village, serves tangy tangomonium yogurt with mango and mochi toppings.
review: Red Mango in Houston’s West University is a Rice Village gem! Visited on a hot night, and this global franchise was packed with a cozy vibe despite limited seating.

name: Refresqueria at Rice Village
description: When Houston heat hits hard, Refresqueria at Rice Village offers the ultimate cool down with bold, fruity flavor and fun Mexican treats.
review: I like this spot and it’s pretty refreshing like it’s namesake. They have soo many colorful fruit flavors and various ice cream. It feels like home in Rice Village. Vibrant and joyful for hot summer days.

name: Rice University Farmers Market
description: Discover fresh Houston farmers market treasures at Rice University Farmers Market in West University. Offering fresh eggs and crusty artisan bread, this Tuesday market is perfect for foodies and eco conscious shoppers.
review: Located around the beautiful and historic Rice University.. I love Tuesday’s Rice Market! I have sampled breads, cheeses, and milks at this location.

name: Richmond Bone & Joint Clinic
description: Richmond Bone & Joint Clinic on Southwest Freeway offers professional medical services for Houston area residents. This modern facility specializes in joint and bone treatments, with a team of doctors ready to assist.
review: Just okay. The whole staff at Richmond Bone & Joint Clinic seemed in a rush, including the doctors. It was a meh experience with a huge price tag. Really wish they showed more care for their patients.

name: Richmond’s Air
description: When Houston’s chilly winters strike, Richmond’s Air is the go to for reliable heating and air conditioning services across the city.
review: I highly recommend Richmond’s Air for all things related to air conditioning and heating. Our upstairs heater broke down & in this cold and frigid season we needed our system back up and running as soon as possible.

name: Roast & Brew
description: Roast & Brew brings a refreshing, airy charm to the Heights, a café designed for comfort, conversation, and creativity.
review: Roast and Brew is such a stellar coffee shop! I love the open air seating and bright natural light pouring through the windows.

name: Rocky Creek Dental Care
description: Rocky Creek Dental Care in Missouri City offers a range of dental services, from general cleanings to cosmetic procedures, catering to Houston area families.
review: I wouldn’t recommend this spot. They are not honest.. albeit they did great work on my teeth. It’s the after charges that they try to push on their current clients. Nope. I don’t think so. Steer clear from this dentistry.

name: Ruchi’s Indian Cuisine
description: Spring Branch may not be the first neighborhood that comes to mind for standout Indian food, but Ruchi’s Indian Cuisine is changing that narrative in the best way possible.
review: I don't think this restaurant has even been opened for a year but man it’s poppin’, the flavors, the service, everything. This gem of a spot is located within the Spring Branch area…

name: Ruggles Café Bakery
description: Ruggles Café Bakery, a welcoming spot in Houston’s West University on Rice Boulevard, offers black bean burgers and rich domino cake.
review: Ruggles Café Bakery in West University was a hit! Came in with six friends on a cold Wednesday night and lucked out with their entree + dessert deal. We ordered sandwiches, burgers, and pasta, everyone loved their meals.

name: Rustika Cafe & Bakery
description: Discover international flavors at Rustika Cafe & Bakery in Houston’s West University, tucked near Kirby Drive. This cozy café specializes in Argentinian empanadas, alfajores, and dulce de leche coffee, alongside muffins and crepes.
review: Nice little café at Rustika Cafe & Bakery, tucked on the outskirts of Kirby near Rice Village.

name: Sabai Thai Cafe
description: Sabai Thai Cafe in Sugar Land serves fragrant pad thai and spicy curry noodle soup in a relaxing ambiance. A gem for Sugar Land Thai lovers, Sabai’s pad thai is a tangy delight, and the curry noodle soup packs a flavorful punch.
review: Ah! Sabai! It’s been my spot for delicious Thai food for four years?! Wow, time flies. The restaurant has undergone design and change over the years. Nonetheless, I still enjoy the ambiance.

name: Saffron Persian Cafe
description: Saffron Persian Cafe, an upstairs spot in Houston’s Gulfton at Hillcroft Plaza, serves Afghan mantu and Persian kebabs with fragrant rice.
review: Saffron Persian Cafe in Houston’s Gulfton is a gem upstairs at Hillcroft Plaza! Serving Afghan and Persian cuisine, it’s a cultural journey with well displayed decor.

name: Saigon Pho and Grill
description: Savor fresh Vietnamese flavors at Saigon Pho and Grill in Sugar Land, a clean, spacious spot on Highway 6 with classical music and colorful dishes like tofu banh mi and vermicelli bowls.
review: Pretty decent Vietnamese food at Saigon Pho and Grill in a clean, spacious spot with classical music, love that vibe! Been here twice, and it’s good, though Pho Ben’s my Sugar Land favorite.

name: Seiwa Market
description: Seiwa Market is a tidy, well organized specialty grocer focused entirely on Japanese products.
review: I like this market! It’s a small specialty shop with exclusively Japanese products. Always clean, always organized, and never overly scented. The produce is hit or miss, cilantro was limp, but cherry tomatoes were vibrant.

name: Sephora at Kohl’s
description: The Sephora at Kohl’s in Westchase brings a refreshing twist to the traditional Sephora experience, calmer, cleaner, less crowded, and wonderfully convenient.
review: So this is a new location of Sephora and they have been open since June 2023. Walk inside Kohl's and you'll spot Sephora's fairly decent sized kiosk store to the left side of the store.

name: Sharetea
description: Dive into authentic Taiwanese bubble tea at Sharetea in Houston’s vibrant Chinatown, located on Bellaire Boulevard.
review: Lovely authentic Taiwanese style tapioca drinks at Sharetea! Boba originated in Taiwan, so they’re doing it right. This Chinatown café is small, brightly lit, with plenty of tables and chairs.

name: Sharetea
description: Cool off with a refreshing drink at Sharetea, a vibrant bubble tea spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6. This lively shop serves crisp tapioca milk tea, cocoa milk, and customizable smoothies, perfect for warm Houston nights.
review: Yay, welcome to the neighborhood, Sharetea! So glad to have you in Sugar Land, this town just got sweeter! Visited around 9:30 pm on New Year’s Eve with my sisters, happy they were open late.

name: Shipley Do-Nuts
description: Satisfy your donut cravings at Shipley Do Nuts in Houston’s Memorial area, a 24 hour spot conveniently located off the freeway.
review: Donuts were old and cold. Greasy and stale upon holding the darn donut. Although known to be 24 hrs, this location totally does not serve warm nor fresh donuts.

name: Shipley Do-Nuts
description: Shipley Do Nuts in Sugar Land, tucked in a quaint plaza on Eldridge Road, serves crispy butterfly rolls, apple fritters, and classic cake donuts.
review: Some of my favorite donuts are at this Shipley Do Nuts in Sugar Land! It’s in a clean, quaint plaza close to everything, one of my favorite spots to stroll.

name: Shogi Hibachi Express
description: Shogi Hibachi Express in Sugar Land offers a unique build your own hibachi bowl with sizzling meats, fresh vegetables, and bold Sichuan sauce.
review: Mm hibachi! & double thumbs up for express! This place has an awesome concept. I recently came in here for lunch with a group of friends. We were seated promptly, and had the best service.

name: Six Ping
description: Six Ping, a tidy bakery in Houston’s Chinatown on Bellaire Boulevard, serves moist coconut bread and flaky croissants.
review: Six Ping in Houston’s Chinatown is a tidy bakery in a bustling shopping district. Their sweet breads are moist, flaky, and lightly sweetened, perfect!

name: Slim Chickens
description: Slim Chickens is one of those spots you see scattered across Houston, often enticing enough to spark curiosity and high expectations. While the concept is promising and the menu broad, not everything hit the mark this time around.
review: Hmm Slim Chickens! More like the bare bones of it. A place that I had high expectations for, but to be honest, those expectations fell flat upon first sight and bite.

name: Slowpokes
description: Slowpokes’ Upper Kirby outpost brings the brand’s signature laid back charm right across from Levy Park.
review: Digging this second location of Slowpokes and liking how it's nestled within the inner loop. The location is stellar, right across Levy park with plenty of parking situated within the garage.

name: Soju Bar
description: Soju Bar brings the energy of a late night Korean drinking den, bold flavors, hearty portions, and a casual, dimly lit atmosphere fit for hanging out after hours.
review: Service is completely non existent at this late night spot. It’s a Korean style bar/restaurant serving decent food with large portions and equally large prices, but the service is sorely disappointing.

name: Soliz Casa De Tacos
description: Start your day at Soliz Casa De Tacos in Stafford known for breakfast tacos and hearty menudo.
review: I don’t wanna taco bout’ it.. but these tacos were muy malo (really bad). My twin sister and I visited Soliz Casa De Tacos last week after running a few errands.

name: SomiSomi
description: SomiSomi in Katy delivers the kind of soft serve experience that’s equal parts nostalgic, playful, and indulgently creamy.
review: SomiSomi Is so so yummy yummy. I'm liking this location out in Katy. A little small within the interior, but most locations seem to be that way. It's a grab and go ice cream spot that fills up quickly.

name: Southern Maid Donuts
description: Start your morning with crispy, fresh donuts at Southern Maid Donuts in Sugar Land, a cozy spot on Eldridge Road.
review: Crisp and fresh donuts at Southern Maid Donuts! Stopped by the other day and grabbed a few cake donuts and old fashioned donuts. The plain cake was my favorite, nice and simple.

name: Southside Espresso
description: Southside Espresso, a cozy spot in Houston’s Montrose on Westheimer Road, serves smooth almond lattes and homemade brownies.
review: Southside Espresso in Montrose was packed on a cold, windy Sunday night, but so cozy! I’d wanted to try this Houston spot since summer and finally made it with my sisters to meet a friend.

name: Sprinkles Houston Westheimer
description: Sprinkles Houston Westheimer in Highland Village is a beloved dessert destination, known for its iconic cupcakes and 24/7 ATM cupcake machine.
review: Oh Sprinkles, Your cupcakes have become drier than a boring brick wall. What happened? Within the span of two months I have visited twice.

name: Starbucks
description: This new Starbucks near Meadows Place brings a fresh, modern, and spotless vibe to a growing corner of Stafford.
review: I don't typically write reviews on Starbucks… but this is a brand new location right by Meadows Place in Stafford. It’s in the same plaza as Aldi. This Starbucks is very clean, quaint, and minimal.

name: Starbucks
description: Zip through your day with a warm café misto at Starbucks in Sugar Land, the only location in the area with a convenient drive thru.
review: This is probably one of the better locations of Starbucks in the Sugar Land area. I’m not the biggest fan of SB, but I appreciate this location in regards to their convenience and service.

name: Sterling McCall Nissan
description: Trust your car to Sterling McCall Nissan in Stafford, a dependable spot on Southwest Freeway for Houston area drivers.
review: Great service and always reliable at Sterling McCall Nissan! Had a maintenance check up a couple of days ago for my Nissan Versa Note, which I got here two years ago.

name: Sugar Land Memorial Park
description: Sugar Land Memorial Park offers a peaceful retreat tucked just far enough from the bustle of daily life.
review: Calm. Clean. Crystal clear. I'm describing this park and the water that stretches throughout the land it's situated on. Very peaceful. You can go fishing near the water or just reflect upon life.

name: Sugar Thai Fine Cuisine
description: Sugar Thai Fine Cuisine, a quaint spot in Sugar Land on University Boulevard, serves less greasy Pad Kee Mao noodles.
review: Sugar Thai Fine Cuisine in Sugar Land is a quaint, new Thai spot among Houston’s cultural restaurants. I ordered Pad Kee Mao noodles, less greasy than most Thai places and flavorful, but too spicy for me.

name: Sunday Press
description: Sunday Press is a vibrant, joyful café that feels like a burst of color from the moment you walk in.
review: My gosh, the menu here is so colorful, fun and quite extensive. You will find something for everyone here! Rejoice. This colorful café in more ways than one is serving up colorful, sweet and intricate food items.

name: SusieCakes
description: Step into the vibrant, retro world of SusieCakes in Houston’s West University, a classic all American bakery that sparkles in Rice Village.
review: What a beautiful, vibrant and retro bakery! This classic all American bakery has arrived to Houston via Nor’Cal. I had heard about SusieCakes via Instagram and had stumbled upon it on my walk through Rice Village.

name: Sweet Lola Yogurt Bar
description: Sweet Lola Yogurt Bar, a cute boutique in Houston’s Fourth Ward near Midtown Plaza, serves creamy royal pear yogurt with fresh toppings.
review: Sweet Lola Yogurt Bar in Houston’s Fourth Ward is the cutest yogurt boutique! Visited after brunch at Coco’s next door, both the exterior and interior are stunning, with lavish candles and stationary.

name: SweetCup
description: Savor local gelato at SweetCup in Houston’s Montrose, a cozy spot on Westheimer Road offering unique flavors like malai kulfi with cardamom. Friendly staff and pizzelle cookies make it a charming stop for Houston gelato fans.
review: SweetCup in Montrose serves local, fresh gelato, but I wasn’t wowed. I’d been dying to visit, but my Saturday evening stop disappointed. Most flavors were nearly gone and looked too soft, like they’d been scooped all day.

name: Tacos A Go Go
description: Tacos A Go Go, a quirky spot in Houston’s Midtown on Main Street, serves vegetarian and fish tacos with addictive peach salsa.
review: Tacos A Go Go in Houston’s Midtown is a fun taco shack! The tacos are good, not amazing, but the vibe is great for chilling with friends. Loved the burst of colors, blue walls with symbols and a cool lady in hat entrance.

name: Tacos Doña Lena
description: Tacos Doña Lena is one of those unassuming neighborhood gems where the food speaks louder than the décor.
review: Absolutely amazing tacos in this hole in the wall joint. Zesty food made by zesty and kind folk. Some of their food took me back to the Yucatán peninsula. The comida takes time to get to the table, but it’s worth it.

name: Taizzi Sushi
description: Taizzi Sushi brings a warm, unpretentious charm to the Katy dining scene.
review: Roll with the tides! Taizzi Sushi in Katy isn't too far from the local mall. Decided to stop by on a whim with a good friend for dinner. I thought the food here was pretty decent.

name: Tasti D Lite
description: Tasti D Lite, a delightful spot in Houston’s Galleria on Post Oak Boulevard, serves creamy mocha almond fudge and green tea soft serve.
review: Tasti D Lite in Houston’s Galleria is a soft serve gem! Love having a soft serve spot in Houston, grew up with it. The guilt free flavors are superb, with lots of toppings to choose.

name: Tea Bar & Organics
description: Tea Bar & Organics, a lively café in Houston’s Chinatown on Bellaire Boulevard, serves hot honey milk tea in cute mugs.
review: Tea Bar & Organics in Chinatown is the original location, way bigger than Sugar Land’s, with tons of seating. I love this spot in the heart of Bellaire, perfect after shopping nearby.

name: Tea Bar and Organics
description: Tea Bar and Organics, a convenient spot in Sugar Land on University Boulevard, offers milk teas and herbal brews. A local stop for Houston area bubble tea fans seeking a quick sip.
review: I’ve visited Tea Bar and Organics in Sugar Land since they opened, but I’m done for good. It’s conveniently located and open late, which is rare around here, so I’d stop by occasionally.

name: Teacake Factory
description: Teacake Factory, a cozy spot in Sugar Land on Highway 6, serves moist strawberry teacakes and nutty delight cake.
review: Teacake Factory in Sugar Land is a Houston area gem, despite some harsh reviews! Their Southern teacakes are moist, flavorful, and made with fresh fruits and nuts, only $2 for a big, shareable treat!

name: Teahouse & Coffee Tapioca Bar
description: Teahouse & Coffee Tapioca Bar in Sugar Land serves flavorful tapioca pearls and rich coffee blends in a cozy coffeehouse setting.
review: I’ve had good experiences at the Tea & Coffee house. The flavours are sweet, and you can actually taste them! The pearls are semi chewy and soft, just the way they should be.

name: Tealicious Drinks
description: Tealicious Drinks, a convenient spot in Houston’s Third Ward on a university campus, serves mango black tea with tapioca and vegetarian banh mi.
review: Tealicious Drinks in Houston’s Third Ward is a campus lifesaver! After hot walks, their cool drinks refresh. Tried most tapioca drinks, mango black tea is my favorite, blending juice and tea perfectly.

name: Teapresso Bar
description: Teapresso Bar in Sugar Land brings a Hawaiian inspired twist to the local café scene, offering Kona coffee, milk teas, hot beverages, and customizable drinks with organic coffee beans, something not easily found in this part of town.
review: This spot was unusually warm today and the service was mediocre at best; which seems to be the case lately. I've always liked Teapresso and really dig the location out in the Heights.. (if it's still around).

name: Terry Hershey Park
description: Terry Hershey Park is one of Houston’s most beloved green escapes, an expansive, tree lined sanctuary tucked right into the bustle of the Energy Corridor.
review: A rather large yet cozy park smacked in the middle of the energy corridor. There are various entrances to reach this park; & yet each entrance happens to guide you through a unique path.

name: Texas Art Supply
description: Unleash your creativity at Texas Art Supply in Houston’s Montrose, a sprawling store packed with art mediums, colorful gifts, and supplies for every artist.
review: So it looks as if i’m the 100th reviewer for this art supply store.. Well.. here we go. What can I say? This store was underwhelming and overwhelming in so may ways.

name: Thai Orchid
description: Thai Orchid brings bold heat, vibrant flavors, and a menu that stretches beyond traditional Thai fare into memorable Laotian and Cambodian dishes.
review: This restaurant really brought in the heat. I thought I could handle any spice level until I met Thai Orchid on a random Sunday night. The best items on the menu are definitely the Laotian and Cambodian influenced dishes.

name: Thai Siam
description: Thai Siam, a cozy spot in Sugar Land on University Boulevard, serves spicy green curry and addictive sate with peanut sauce.
review: Thai Siam in Sugar Land is a cozy Houston area gem! The traditional Thai decor gives a cultural vibe I love. Pad thai and pad kee mao were flavorful with rice noodles and meats.

name: Thai Spice
description: Thai Spice in Pearland, a quiet spot on Broadway Street, serves delicious crab fried rice and pad thai.
review: Thai Spice in Pearland serves delicious, authentic Thai cuisine, just as good as their Rice Village location! I loved the crab fried rice, pad thai, and fried banana with ice cream, so flavorful.

name: The Afghan Village
description: Explore Afghan flavors at The Afghan Village in Houston’s Gulfton area on Hillcroft Street, offering dishes like mantoo and Uzbaki rice.
review: The Afghan Village’s food didn’t live up to the hype, I’ve had better Afghan elsewhere. The Uzbaki rice was too soft, and the spinach was watery and tasteless.

name: The Cheesecake Factory
description: Indulge in Houston desserts at The Cheesecake Factory in Galleria/Uptown, where rich chocolate cake and a vibrant international ambiance await.
review: I love how there is an upstairs to this location! The place is nicely laid out. I tried the chocolate cake at this spot. The waitress was very nice.

name: The Grove Donutz & Deli
description: The Grove Donutz & Deli offers a mix of nostalgic, simple donuts alongside their well known extravagant “monster” creations.
review: I’m normally not a fan of monster like donuts, the custom ones loaded with crazy ingredients. Fun to look at, creative even, but taste wise? Meh. I’m a simple donut gal.

name: The Moghul’s Restaurant & M Lounge
description: The Moghul’s Restaurant & M Lounge, a spacious spot in Houston’s Westchase on Westheimer Road, serves deep flavored nihari curry and pillowy naan.
review: The Moghul’s in Houston’s Westchase is a South Asian gem! Visited with family, and we loved the huge, airy space with dim, glowing lights at night.

name: The Oceanaire Seafood Room
description: The Oceanaire Seafood Room is a long standing Galleria favorite, known for its sleek, submarine inspired design, large corner windows overlooking bustling streets, and over two decades of reputation as a premier seafood destination.
review: 3 stars experience during Houston Restaurant Weeks. Boy, were we all excited to dine in at this restaurant. It is a Houston classic!

name: The Original Marini’s Empanada House
description: A long loved Houston institution, The Original Marini’s Empanada House delivers warmth, charm, and old world comfort with every crispy, freshly fried empanada.
review: They have cats upon the premises! That's the main reason I dined in here a couple of days ago. Jk. I had dinner here a few nights ago with a good friend.

name: The Port of Peri Peri
description: Spice up your meal at The Port of Peri Peri in Sugar Land, a bustling Houston area spot serving fiery peri peri chicken strips and cassava fries with chili sauce.
review: Porto’s Peri Peri. Double the name. Double the trouble. I dined in here last night with my sister and cousin. The restaurant was completely full to the brim with people rushing in and dining with their large families.

name: The Sweet Boutique Bakery
description: The Sweet Boutique Bakery, a charming spot in Sugar Land on University Boulevard, serves exotic rose macaroons and creme brulee cupcakes.
review: The Sweet Boutique Bakery in Sugar Land is a Houston area gem!

name: The Teahouse Tapioca & Tea
description: Sip on refreshing bubble tea at The Teahouse Tapioca & Tea in Sugar Land, a Houston area favorite offering creamy milk teas and customizable tapioca drinks.
review: [Note: No review text was provided for The Teahouse Tapioca & Tea.

name: The Waffle Bus
description: The Waffle Bus, a popular food truck in Houston’s The Heights near University of Houston, serves nutella and banana waffle sandwiches.
review: The Waffle Bus in Houston’s The Heights finally hit University of Houston! Tried it two days in a row despite the hot wait.

name: Thierry André Tellier Café
description: Thierry André Tellier Café, tucked in Uptown Park, delights with flaky almond croissants and delicate petit fours.
review: Aw, what a cute little patisserie! Those were the words that came out of my mouth as I found this little gem, tucked in Uptown Park. I have only came in here on a few visits to pick up sweets.

name: Third Gen Coffee
description: Tucked beneath a canopy of trees along Grogan’s Drive, Third Gen Coffee feels like a cozy escape, a quiet, woodsy nook with nostalgic winter charm and the warmth of a true neighborhood café.
review: Such a great little coffee shoppe tucked in the Woodlands on Grograns drive. I'm diggin' this quiet little corner, cluttered with trees and a few stores lined up together.

name: Three Brothers Bakery
description: Step into old fashioned charm at Three Brothers Bakery in Houston’s Braeswood Place on South Braeswood Boulevard.
review: Lovely old fashioned bakery at Three Brothers in Braeswood Place, loaded with wonderful baked goods! I think this is the original location, sadly, the Sugar Land one closed years ago, which was so convenient.

name: Throughgood Coffee
description: Sip a decadent cappuccino at Throughgood Coffee in Houston’s The Heights, a quaint cafe with glowing lights and a nearby taco truck.
review: Throughgood Coffee is tucked in a quaint and cozy neighborhood in the Heights. I’m liking the vibe of this cafe and how its within walking reach in a quiet neighborhood.

name: Tiff’s Treats
description: Tiff’s Treats, a popular spot in Houston’s Greenway on Weslayan Street, bakes fresh cookies like chocolate chip and butterscotch.
review: Heard a lot about Tiff’s Treats in Houston’s Greenway, so I got a Groupon. Sadly, the cookies, white chocolate & almond, brownie, chocolate chip, M&M, and butterscotch, were too sweet and salty, even for my sweet tooth.

name: Tim Hortons
description: Tucked into a quiet corner of town, this cozy café offers a nostalgic, no fuss approach to coffee and baked treats, a welcome change from trend heavy cafés.
review: Such a great little gem of a coffee shoppe tucked in a quiet corner within the suburbs of Katy, TX. Tim Horton's is originally from Canada.. & is all the rage up in the northern hemisphere... & I can totally see why!

name: Tim Hortons
description: Step into the cozy, quick stop charm of Tim Hortons in Stafford, a compact corner café near Meadows Place that delivers big on seasonal flavor.
review: Halloween spooky flavors are here… such as their collab with anything Reese’s PB flavors and all things autumnal pumpkin spice. They also have Halloween TimBits buckets for all things trick or treat.

name: Torchy's Tacos
description: Torchy's Tacos in Sugar Land on Town Center Boulevard serves up creative tacos with heaps of shredded cheese and spicy salsas. Ideal for Tex Mex fans, Torchy's is.
review: Cold and salty food at Torchy's Tacos. Tons of shredded cheese seemed to hide the flavor. Mediocre taste overall. I had a feeling this Sugar Land location wouldn’t have the best tacos.

name: Torchy’s Tacos
description: Torchy’s Tacos, a lively spot in Houston’s West University on Rice Boulevard, serves flavorful Mr. Pink salmon tacos. Pink taco for a zesty bite.
review: Mm mm… yum! Torchy’s Tacos in West University is a Houston gem with mean, flavorful tacos! Thrilled they opened in Rice Village, it completes the area’s unique eateries. I got the Mr.

name: Tout Suite
description: Tout Suite, a chic warehouse turned café in Houston’s Warehouse District on Commerce Street, offers cream cheese danishes, cupcakes, and creamy lattes.
review: Tout Suite in the Warehouse District is a cool warehouse turned dessert café! Visited around 9 pm with a friend and felt safe inside, despite the random downtown location. It’s far from home, but worth the trip.

name: Tree House
description: Cool off at Tree House in Houston’s Energy Corridor, a cute café on Dairy Ashford Road blending frozen yogurt and coffee.
review: Nice, new, and cute spot at Tree House! Love the concept, frozen yogurt and coffee together? Awesome! Visited recently and went for the froyo, choosing cake batter and vanilla.

name: Turquoise Grill & Bar
description: Turquoise Grill & Bar, a long standing spot in Sugar Land on University Boulevard, offers Turkish and Greek dishes. Try a Turkish dish for a savory bite.
review: I’ve been coming to Turquoise Grill & Bar in Sugar Land for a couple of years, but the food and service have really gone downhill. The dishes are skimpy, cold, and unappealing now, which is such a shame.

name: Tutti Frutti
description: Tutti Frutti in Sugar Land is one of the last remaining froyo staples in the area, and while its classic self serve setup remains familiar, the menu has expanded with fun additions like bubble waffles and smoothies.
review: Surprise surprise… they are now serving bubble waffles and smoothies here. Smelled delightful upon entering this bright spot. Seems as if they've gotten really busy over time.

name: Tutti Frutti Frozen Yogurt
description: Tutti Frutti Frozen Yogurt, a clean spot in Missouri City on FM 1092, serves coconut and lychee yogurt in a colorful setting.
review: I’ve been coming to Tutti Frutti Frozen Yogurt in Missouri City for years, and it’s always clean, no sticky floors or pumps, which I love. The colorful interior and chairs add a fun vibe.

name: Tutti Frutti Frozen Yogurt
description: : “Surprise surprise… they are now serving bubble waffles and smoothies here. Smelled delightful upon entering this bright spot. Seems as if they've gotten really busy over time.
review: I love the fact that there are fruity and non fruity flavours to choose from at Tutti Frutti. I recently checked out this establishment on a hot afternoon day.

name: Té House of Tea
description: Té House of Tea, a quaint spot in Houston’s Montrose on Fairview Street, offers global teas like metropolis and vegan sweet potato soup.
review: Té House of Tea in Montrose is a Houston gem for tea lovers like me! The global tea selection is lovely, and my friend and I shared the fragrant, light metropolis tea, enough in the kettle for both of us.

name: t’afia
description: t’afia, a lively spot in Houston’s Midtown on Travis Street, serves egg and ham biscuit sandwiches with local produce.
review: t’afia in Houston’s Midtown is a gem, ‘to your health!’ Chef Monica Pope’s brilliance shines with local produce and free Saturday cooking classes.

name: Universal Bakery and Snacks
description: Universal Bakery and Snacks in Sugar Land on Highway 6 is a vibrant spot for Indian street food like vada pav, spicy chaat, and puff pastries.
review: Yum! The vada pav at Universal Bakery and Snacks is so good! I was craving a spicy, crispy potato sandwich, and that’s exactly what I got. Love those carb on carb vegetarian vibes!

name: Van Leeuwen Ice Cream
description: Bright, cheerful, and sweetly satisfying, Van Leeuwen in Montrose is a delightful stop for anyone craving premium ice cream with creative flair.
review: Loved this little sweet elite perk! This ice cream spot is bright and cheery, perfect on this sunny Saturday visit. I've been to V.L.

name: Vasos Little Greek Kitchen
description: Indulge in smooth lattes and Greek pastries at Vasos Little Greek Kitchen in Sugar Land, a cozy Houston area cafe with rainbow cookies and Italian origin coffee.
review: I really enjoyed visiting Vasos Little Greek Kitchen earlier in the summer. They took over a coffee house previously known as Anonymous Cafe. For quite a few months this little space was unoccupied.

name: Verbena Coffee
description: Verbena Coffee is a warm, wood toned retreat tucked into the Memorial/Energy Corridor area, a neighborhood café that has quickly grown into a beloved local staple.
review: Such a great little coffee shop in the neighborhood, and it hasn’t even been open for two years. They’re thriving in the Memorial area and it’s wonderful supporting local.

name: Viva Juice Coffee & Tea
description: Viva Juice Coffee & Tea in Houston’s Alief, a cozy café on Bellaire Boulevard, serves sweet, chewy coffee milk tea with tapioca. Sip a coffee milk tea for a sweet pick me up.
review: Dropped into Viva Juice Coffee & Tea in Alief after a dentist appointment to kill time before work. Thanh greeted me kindly and was super patient as I picked my order.

name: Voodoo Doughnut
description: Voodoo Doughnut brings its signature pink flair and eccentric personality to Houston, but the experience doesn’t quite match the magic of its flagship locations in Portland or Austin.
review: The doughnuts here aren’t as fresh as the Austin location. They’re not churning through batches the way they do in PDX or ATX, so things get a bit stale. The storefront lacks the charm of the original shops too.

name: Voodoo Doughnut
description: Voodoo Doughnut on East 6th Street in Downtown Austin is your 24/7 haven for quirky, delicious donuts.
review: This doughnut shop tucked on east 6th street is open 24 hours 7 days of the week! When you have a hankering for doughnuts.. this place will always be there for you.

name: Walmart Supercenter
description: Shop with ease at Walmart Supercenter in Sugar Land, a massive Houston area store with organic baking goods, car products, and a McDonald’s inside.
review: Walmart somehow reminds me of highschool. You’re embarrassed to be there and it’s a warped trip down memory lane. The bright fluorescent lights and the dull atmosphere.

name: WEST on WEST
description: WEST on WEST, affectionately known as WoW, has quickly transformed from an empty lot into one of Westchase’s most vibrant up and coming shopping plazas.
review: I remember when Mark pointed out WoW plaza back in 2023... it was an empty lot. We were hanging out that day, running on some Trader Joe's errands. Lol. Fast forward and I have had the chance to visit WoW twice so far...

name: Whit N Wingo
description: Whit N Wingo is the kind of vintage shop that immediately pulls you in with its color, charm, and treasure hunt energy.
review: Quite a unique vintage shoppe, very colorful with so many items on display and for purchase. I found a few cute rings here and I just love wearing them.

name: Whole Foods Market
description: Explore a foodie paradise at Whole Foods Market in Sugar Land, offering black bean enchiladas and steaming fresh soup.
review: I love Whole Foods! Thankful to have a great selection in Sugar Land. I frequent this market often. I have never been disappointed. It is an epicureans dream!

name: World Market
description: World Market in Stafford offers a vibrant, culturally rich escape, perfect for anyone who thrives on global flavors, décor, and eclectic treasures.
review: It is wonderful to explore this culturally diverse store during limited moments of traveling. Anything cultural and world related excites the heck out of me. Thank y’all for opening this store during such obscure times.

name: Yogurtland
description: Yogurtland in Memorial City Mall offers a reliably sweet stop for those craving creamy frozen yogurt with fresh, colorful toppings.
review: Solid location of Yogurtland. Although located in the mall, this spot offers plenty of flavors that are delectable with fresh toppings.

name: Yogurtland Houston
description: Yogurtland Houston, a vibrant spot in Houston’s Galleria on Westheimer Road, offers a plethora of frozen yogurt flavors like dutch chocolate and coconut.
review: Yogurtland Houston in the Galleria is a frozen yogurt paradise! With so many flavors, you can’t go wrong.

name: Yomie’s Rice X Yogurt
description: Yomie’s Rice X Yogurt brings a unique concept to Chinatown with its lineup of creamy, rice based and yogurt based beverages.
review: Service was super awkward, cold, and dry, just like the cutting winds outside that night. The drinks were okay: simple yogurt based beverages that were creamy and mellow.

name: Yummy’s Hot Chicken
description: Yummy’s Hot Chicken takes the ever popular hot chicken trend and elevates it with a bold Syrian twist. This unassuming food truck delivers layers of flavor, crunch, and spice that set it apart from the typical fried chicken lineup.
review: Hot. Crispy. Chicken sandwich. But with a Syrian twist. This sandwich was *hecka* good, lots of flavor, layers, and textures. Yummy’s has a small, simple menu, but every item overdelivers.

name: Zeyad Bakery & Sweets
description: Indulge in Palestinian delights at Zeyad Bakery & Sweets in Houston, a hidden gem serving creamy baklava and savory spinach pies.
review: A shabby and rundown strip on Richmond Ave.. Zeyad Bakery & Sweets offers up some savory and sweet Palestinian baked goods. The outside of the bakery gives off an unkempt and uninviting feel.

name: Zoa Moroccan Kitchen
description: Zoa Moroccan Kitchen has built a name for itself across Houston with fast casual Moroccan bowls, customizable toppings, and comforting warm flavors.
review: This was the third Zoa Moroccan Kitchen location that I have visited within Houston. They have locations all around the city and are rather convenient for visiting over lunch or dinner. So far with this location?
